message.content:
Work in /opt/nxeon. Write the definitive internal manual for **Nxeon**, a Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform (Next.js App Router + Prisma/Postgres + a systemd worker + Proxmox + Mailcow). Two previous attempts at this were cut off before writing anything, so start fresh and WRITE EARLY — save progress to the file as you go rather than composing everything before your first write.

YOU OWN: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` and new files under `docs/`. Do NOT edit `docs/AUDIT-24H.md`, `docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md`, `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` — read them, they are goldmines. Do NOT edit ANY source file. Several agents are changing code concurrently, so describe what you read and cite where.

RENDERING TARGET — read `app/admin/docs/page.tsx` and `lib/markdown.ts` FIRST:
- Rendered at `/admin/docs`; the viewer **splits at every `##` (H2)** into a searchable section list, so H2s ARE the navigation. Pick them as things someone would search for.
- Supported: headings, bold, italic, inline code, fenced code blocks, lists, blockquotes, links, rules, and **GitHub tables** (support added recently — use them freely).
- NOT supported: mermaid, images, raw HTML, nested lists (they render flat — restructure instead).
- So draw every diagram, screen layout and workflow as **ASCII/box art in fenced code blocks**, under ~100 columns.

PRODUCE:
1. Keep the existing dated change-log entries; restructure so reference material leads and history sits in a clearly-marked later part.
2. Front section: what Nxeon is; an ASCII architecture diagram (web / worker / Proxmox / Postgres / Mailcow / nginx); request and job lifecycles; environments (prod `/opt/nxeon`, staging `/opt/nxeon-staging`).
3. Per-feature chapters — what it does, ASCII wireframe of the customer screen, ASCII workflow, real `file:line` entry points, data model, failure modes, how an admin diagnoses it. Cover: deploy wizard; plans/terms; wallet, checkout, wallet/card split; invoices; **renewals + card auto-charge + dunning** (`worker/billing.ts` — wallet credit first, card for the remainder, retries days 1/3/5, and `Server.suspendReason` UNPAID vs ABUSE vs ADMIN and why it exists); server lifecycle; resize and **proration** (`lib/proration.ts` — one shared function so displayed = charged = credited); disk expansion; volumes; backups (daily, keep 3, `/tank/backup/platform` kept separate from customer archives so a customer prune cannot delete platform ones, plus restore verification); snapshots/restore; **server migration** — the flagship, deepest chapter, including the verification gate and `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES`; control panel; web console; SFTP; domains, transfer-in and the markup setting; Cloudflare OAuth; SSL lifecycle; Nxeon Mail; business email + DKIM; game servers; Build with AI; teams; support; notifications; API tokens; 2FA (note `lib/totp-verify.ts` is a PLAIN module deliberately — exported from a `"use server"` file it was a public brute-force oracle); growth; bandwidth; admin surfaces; RBAC.
4. Admin runbooks: deploying; restarting safely (**never restart the worker while a job is RUNNING** — show the queue check); reading worker logs; diagnosing a stuck job; re-running a failed migration; issuing a cert by hand; checking mail deliverability — including that this box's `/etc/hosts` + `nsswitch: files myhostname dns` makes the system resolver answer reverse lookups from a local file, so deliverability checks MUST query authoritative nameservers; rolling back.
5. Troubleshooting: symptom → cause → fix tables mined from the field notes and both audits.
6. Data model reference from `prisma/schema.prisma`.
7. **A "known gaps / not true yet" section — the most valuable part.** There is one recurring defect in this codebase: a surface reporting an outcome it never verified. Today alone: SSL wrote certificate rows ACTIVE with invented expiries while no certbot ran; game settings notified "applied" with nothing written; the migration logged "Sites actually serving: 4/4" with six domains dark; the admin domain markup displayed 0% while customers were charged 25%; the auto-suspend kill switch was saved and read by nothing. Several are now fixed, several are not. Document what is genuinely true, what is simulated, and what is saved-but-unread — honestly. Docs that overclaim would be the same bug in a new place.

METHOD: investigate before writing; every `file:line` must be real; never invent behaviour. If unsure, read it; if still unclear, write what you verified and flag the gap.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Documentation only. Do NOT edit source. Do NOT run `npm run build`/`dev`, do NOT restart services, do NOT git commit/push. Read-only DB inspection is fine.

Report: the H2 structure, roughly how much you wrote, and anything documented-but-wrong you corrected.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
17	- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
18	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
19	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).
20	
21	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
22	
23	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
24	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
25	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
26	
27	## Conventions
28	
29	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
30	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
31	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
32	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
33	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
34	
35	## Documentation — keep it current (required)
36	
37	- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
38	- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
39	- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
40	- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.
41	
42	## Commands
43	
44	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
45	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
46	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
47	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
48	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
49	
50	## Domains & TLS
51	
52	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
53	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
54	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP.
55	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
56	
57	## Environments
58	
59	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
60	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
61	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
62	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.
63	
64	## Safety rules
65	
66	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
67	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
68	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
69	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
70	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
71	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.
72

1	# Customer Migration — Field Notes & Failure Catalog
2	
3	Real-world failures observed running the lift-and-shift migration against a live
4	customer server, with the fix for each. **This is the acceptance criteria for the
5	migration engine**: a customer should be able to migrate, point DNS, and have their
6	site serve over HTTPS with no server access.
7	
8	Source of truth for these findings: a real migration on 2026-07-25 from a
9	HestiaCP/Hostinger box (Debian, nginx 1.25, 72.62.69.9) to a fresh Nxeon VPS
10	(Ubuntu 22.04, nginx 1.18, 1 vCPU / 2 GB / 25 GB).
11	
12	---
13	
14	## The architectural lesson
15	
16	**Do not blind-copy the source's `/etc/nginx` (or `/etc/apache2`) tree.** That single
17	behaviour caused roughly half of the failures below. Copying wholesale imports the
18	source's `nginx.conf`, its include layout, its panel-specific vhosts, its IP
19	bindings, and its certificate paths — none of which are valid on the target.
20	
21	Instead:
22	1. **Parse the source vhosts for intent** — server_name(s), document root or upstream
23	   proxy target, port, TLS on/off.
24	2. **Generate clean configs for the target's own web-server version.**
25	3. Leave the target's `nginx.conf` and include layout **intact**.
26	4. Copy the source config tree to a reference dir only
27	   (`/root/nxeon-migrations/<id>/source-nginx/`), never into live config.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## Failure catalog
32	
33	### Web server / routing
34	
35	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
36	|---|---------|---------|-----|
37	| 1 | Source `nginx.conf` overwrote the target's | `include sites-enabled/*` disappeared → a generated vhost is **silently ignored** | Write vhosts where the *live* `nginx.conf` actually includes; verify with `nginx -T \| grep <server_name>`, not just `nginx -t` |
38	| 2 | Hardcoded source IP in ~21 configs | `bind() to <old-ip>:80 failed (99)` — nginx won't start | Rewrite source IP → target IP everywhere, or generate configs without IP binding |
39	| 3 | `/etc/letsencrypt` not migrated | 5 vhosts referenced missing certs + `options-ssl-nginx.conf` → config test fails → **web server down** | Migrate `/etc/letsencrypt` (certs, renewal conf, accounts) **or** strip TLS blocks and re-issue via certbot after DNS points over. Never leave a config referencing a missing cert |
40	| 4 | Web-server version mismatch | `http2 on;` (nginx ≥1.25) is an unknown directive on 1.18 | Detect target nginx version; translate/neutralise incompatible directives |
41	| 5 | Missing log directories | `open() "/var/log/apache2/domains/..." failed` | `mkdir -p` + `touch` every log path a config references before testing |
42	| 6 | Dead catch-all default server | Copied `listen <ip>:80 default; proxy_pass http://<ip>:8080;` hijacked everything → **502 on all traffic** | Detect copied default/catch-all servers whose upstream is dead; disable them |
43	| 7 | `listen` specificity beats `server_name` | An IP-bound block (`listen <ip>:80`) wins over generic `listen 80` regardless of server_name — our vhost never selected. **Repeated on 443** → wrong cert → `ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID` | Generated vhosts must bind the target's public IP explicitly on **both** 80 and 443 when copied configs do |
44	| 8 | Stale nginx PID after config swap | `invalid PID number "" in /var/run/nginx.pid`; `reload` fails | Use `restart` (not `reload`) after replacing nginx.conf; verify `systemctl is-active` |
45	| 9 | Multi-tenant wildcard subdomains | Tenant subdomains hit no server block → wrong cert | Add `server_name *.<domain>` when the app is multi-tenant (e.g. a `*_BASE_DOMAIN` env var). **A wildcard cert needs DNS-01** — HTTP-01 cannot issue `*.domain` |
46	
47	### Application startup
48	
49	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
50	|---|---------|---------|-----|
51	| 10 | Docker **images** not migrated | Standalone containers using locally-built images (`app/frontend:latest`, never in a registry) can never start | `docker save \| gzip` on source → stream → `docker load` on target. Prefer `docker pull` for public-registry images |
52	| 11 | App configured for the **old domain** | `PUBLIC_APP_URL`/`PUBLIC_API_URL` pointed at the old host — and frameworks like Astro/Next **bake the API URL into the static bundle at build time**. Page loads; nothing works | Detect old-hostname references in copied env; offer to rewrite **and rebuild** the affected image. A frontend calling the old server's API is a *silent* failure |
53	| 12 | Secrets in a non-standard env file | compose had `${VAR}` placeholders but no `.env` — real file was `prod.env` (used via `--env-file`) | Detect the env file the project actually uses; if placeholders would resolve empty, **refuse to start** and name the missing vars |
54	| 13 | Absolute binary paths differ between hosts | Migrated systemd units called `/usr/local/bin/node` (manual install on source); target has `/usr/bin/node` (apt) → unit crash-looped **880 times** | Resolve `ExecStart` binaries; symlink or rewrite the unit to the target's real path |
55	| 14 | Framework build artifacts don't transfer | Next.js `.next` copied but had no valid production build → `Could not find a production build` | Detect framework apps and run their build on the target (`next build`), or verify `BUILD_ID` exists before enabling the service |
56	| 15 | MySQL users & grants not migrated | Dump intentionally skips the `mysql` system schema, so **app DB users vanish** → access-denied despite data being present | Enumerate non-system users, `SHOW GRANTS`, replay `CREATE USER`/`GRANT` on the target preserving password hashes. (Postgres `pg_dumpall` already carries roles) |
57	| 16 | Stack-manager deployments | Apps deployed via Dokploy/Coolify/Portainer keep env/secrets in the manager's **own database**, not on disk (`/data/compose/<id>/`) | Detect the layout and warn explicitly — file copy alone will miss the secrets |
58	
59	### Storage / capacity
60	
61	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
62	|---|---------|---------|-----|
63	| 17 | `/var/lib/containerd` is a **separate store** from `/var/lib/docker` | Relocated `/var/lib/docker` to the attached volume; root **still** hit 100% — containerd had grown to 9.4 GB | Relocate/bind-mount **both**; add to `/etc/fstab`; verify with `df -h /var/lib/docker /var/lib/containerd` |
64	| 18 | Build cache is enormous | `docker builder prune -af` reclaimed **7.1 GB** after two builds | Prune after bring-up; retry once after pruning on ENOSPC before failing |
65	| 19 | Attached block volume unused | A 20 GB volume was attached but unformatted/unmounted while root filled | Detect an attached disk with no FSTYPE/mountpoint; format ext4, mount persistently by UUID, relocate the container stores onto it |
66	| 20 | Space estimate ignored Docker overhead | Guardrail estimated the ~11 GB file copy; image pulls/builds blew past it → `no space left on device` killed 2 of 3 compose projects | Include source image bytes + 1.5–2× build/ingest headroom; **re-check free space before the image phase**, not only at start |
67	| 21 | Small targets get starved | On 1 vCPU / 2 GB, a .NET + Astro build starved the box so hard the **QEMU guest agent stopped responding** | Don't assume the guest agent stays reachable during builds; keep the engine's SSH channel authoritative. Warn when target resources are small relative to detected workload |
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Verification bar
72	
73	The final summary must distinguish **"migrated & running (verified)"** from
74	**"copied — needs a manual step"**, and verification must **HTTP-probe the real
75	hostname(s)** — not merely check that a port is listening. Never report success when
76	the site does not actually serve.
77	
78	Where full automation is genuinely impossible, say so **actionably** — name the file,
79	the value, and the command:
80	- wildcard TLS certs (need DNS-01),
81	- compiled-in API URLs (need a rebuild),
82	- stack-manager secrets held in the manager's database,
83	- standalone containers whose images aren't reproducible.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Same-OS question
88	
89	Matching the source OS removes a real class of problems (web-server/package version
90	and config-syntax incompatibilities — items 4 and some of 13), and the wizard
91	recommends it. **It is not a silver bullet**: items 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 14,
92	15, 17–21 are OS-independent migration-completeness issues.
93	
94	---
95	
96	## 2026-07-25 — "reported SUCCESS, customer saw a certificate warning and an Apache default page"
97	
98	A real customer migration completed and reported success. The customer opened their
99	main site and got a browser certificate warning, clicked through it, and landed on
100	the **Apache2 Debian Default Page**. Six of their domains were dark. The run log
101	said `Sites actually serving: 4/4`.
102	
103	Five separate failures, all now closed in `worker/migrate-real.ts`.
104	
105	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix (implemented) |
106	|---|---------|---------|-------------------|
107	| 22 | **The success metric could not fail** | Log line 1: `Sites actually serving: 4/4`. Log line 5: `Sites we could not publish automatically — content.revsports.ca, dealerleads.me, new.nexis.revsports.ca, reel.revsports.ca, stg.studionexis.com, studionexis.com`. The denominator was "domains we chose to publish", so it was 100% by construction | Denominator is now every hostname the **source** served, taken from its own live vhost config before we decide what we can publish (`sourceDomains`). The score is `served/total` against that set, the unserved ones are named, and a run with any unserved domain returns `outcome: "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"` |
108	| 23 | **A 200 from the distribution's default page counted as "serving"** | The existing "make a real request to each domain" probe passed for a domain answering 200 with the Apache2 Debian Default Page | The probe now fetches the **body** as well as the status. Apache "It works!" / "Apache2 Debian Default Page" / "Apache2 Ubuntu Default Page" / "Apache HTTP Server Test Page", nginx "Welcome to nginx!", and empty/near-empty 2xx bodies are all **not serving**. Content is only judged on a 2xx (a 301→HTTPS or a 404 legitimately has a tiny body); short JSON/XML bodies are exempt so an API vhost is never called dark |
109	| 24 | **TLS name mismatch was invisible** | `studionexis.com` was served `nexis.revsports.ca`'s certificate. Every visitor got a full-page security warning before reaching the site — and the probe used `-k`, so it saw only the status code | After each probe the certificate the server actually presents for that name is read with SNI (`openssl s_client -servername`), and its CN/SAN set is matched against the domain (`*.x` covers exactly one label). No coverage ⇒ **not serving**. Skipped when a container owns 443, where the proxy issues its own certificates after DNS moves |
110	| 25 | **`203/EXEC` — unit enabled with a binary that does not exist here** | `nexis-next.service` had `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/node …`; the target has only `/usr/bin/node` (v20, apt). Crash-looped **78 times** and the migration still reported success | **Executable pre-flight before enabling anything.** Every `ExecStart` / `ExecStartPre` / `ExecStartPost` is parsed for its leading absolute executable (handling `-`/`@`/`+`/`!` prefixes, quoted paths, line continuations, `ExecStart=` list resets; PATH-resolved commands ignored). Missing ⇒ symlink to the same basename found via `command -v`, else copy the file from the source, else **do not enable it** and record a blocking entry naming the unit and the path |
111	| 26 | **"Never built" apps crash-loop silently** | `/opt/nexis` had no `.next` production build, so even with Node fixed the unit exits 1 forever | **Health gate after enabling.** Units settle, then `NRestarts` is sampled twice: `active` + a counter that is not climbing, or it is a blocker with the last journal lines attached. The Next.js `Could not find a production build in the '.next' directory` message is recognised by name and answered with `next build` |
112	| 27 | **Two web servers, one port 80** | `apache2` was re-enabled from the source's service list while we generated an nginx config. It could not bind 80 and sat `enabled + failed` — quiet until a reboot, where the race decides whether the site or the default page answers | When we generate our own configuration, every other host web server (`apache2`, `httpd`, `caddy`, `lighttpd` — or `nginx` when we chose Apache) is stopped, **disabled and masked**, and the run says so with the `systemctl unmask` command to reverse it. Step 11 also refuses to re-enable a web server from the source's service list when it is not the one we chose |
113	| 28 | **Ten minutes of silence at 89%** | The progress bar sat frozen while `apt-get install certbot` ran. A wedged migration and a slow one looked identical | The three genuinely long steps — package install, image transfer, certificate issuance — run inside a heartbeat that emits one line every ~45s naming what is still running and for how long |
114	
115	### The point about #25
116	
117	**This failure was already in this document.** It is item 13, written up after an
118	earlier migration where the same `/usr/local/bin/node` mismatch crash-looped a unit
119	880 times, with the fix spelled out: *"Resolve `ExecStart` binaries; symlink or
120	rewrite the unit to the target's real path."*
121	
122	It recurred anyway, on a different customer, four months later — because a documented
123	fix is not a fix. Nothing in the engine read this file. **That is why #25 is now an
124	executable pre-flight check that runs before every `systemctl enable`, not a
125	paragraph.** The general rule this establishes: a failure mode that has been observed
126	twice belongs in code, and a field note describing a fix nobody implemented is worth
127	approximately nothing.
128	
129	### Outcome semantics
130	
131	`runRealMigration` now returns `outcome: "COMPLETED" | "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"` plus
132	`outcomeReasons`, `sourceDomains`, `unservedDomains` and `blockers`. A migration is
133	`COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` when any domain the source served does not serve here, when
134	any domain could not be checked, or when any migrated unit is not running.
135	
136	`Migration.status` in `prisma/schema.prisma` is a plain `String` (not a Prisma enum),
137	but the only writer is `worker/migrate.ts`, which sets `status: "DONE"`
138	unconditionally and persists **only** `summary.results` into `Migration.items.results`.
139	So the outcome is also emitted as the **first entry of `results`** — step
140	`Migration outcome: COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES`, status `failed` — which is what actually
141	reaches the customer's screen today. Wiring `summary.outcome` through to
142	`Migration.status` / a dedicated column is a one-line change in `worker/migrate.ts`
143	that has not been made.

1	# Nxeon — 24-hour session audit
2	
3	Audit of the engineering session transcript `4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc.jsonl`
4	(2026-07-23 09:56 → 2026-07-25 19:58 UTC; the 24-hour window requested by the user is
5	**2026-07-24 19:56 → 2026-07-25 19:56**). Every user instruction and every assistant
6	recommendation in that window was extracted from the transcript and then **verified against the
7	live codebase at `/opt/nxeon`** (HEAD `8e93b13`, `origin/main` in sync).
8	
9	The standard applied throughout: *code existing is not the same as the feature working.* A server
10	action nobody calls, a status computed and then overwritten by its caller, a flag that silently
11	switches a real integration into simulation — all count as **NOT DONE**, regardless of how complete
12	the implementation looks.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## Executive summary
17	
18	### Counts
19	
20	| | User instructions | Assistant recommendations | Total |
21	|---|---|---|---|
22	| **DONE** | 40 | 17 | **57** |
23	| **PARTIAL** | 14 | 8 | **22** |
24	| **NOT DONE** | 6 | 18 | **24** |
25	| **UNCLEAR / external** | 1 | 3 | **4** |
26	| **Declined by user** | — | 1 | **1** |
27	| **Totals** | **61** | **47** | **108** |
28	
29	Headline: the *feature* work of the last 24 hours largely landed. What did not land is the
30	**trust layer** — the places where the platform tells a paying customer something that is not true.
31	Nine of the top ten gaps below are of that kind, and three of them move real money.
32	
33	### CRITICAL — found during this audit, ranks above everything below
34	
35	**Any customer can take over another customer's email domain, reset the password on their live
36	mailboxes, and then read and send mail as them.** This was surfaced by a QA agent still running from
37	the original session (`docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md`) and I verified the whole chain independently:
38	
39	1. `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:254-256` — the "one subscription per domain" check is scoped to the
40	   **caller**: `where: { userId: user.id, domainName: name, … }`. It never asks whether another user
41	   already holds that domain.
42	2. `prisma/schema.prisma:604` — `EmailSubscription.domainName` is a plain `String` with **no
43	   `@unique`**, so the database does not stop it either. `Mailbox.address` (`:623`) is likewise not
44	   unique.
45	3. `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:491-538` `addMailbox` checks only `sub.userId !== user.id`, and its
46	   duplicate check (`:514`) is scoped to *that subscription's own* mailboxes. The attacker can
47	   therefore create `admin@victim.com` under their own subscription. No DNS-verification gate applies.
48	4. `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:684-707` `resetMailboxPassword` validates
49	   `mailbox.subscription.userId !== user.id` — which **passes**, because the row is the attacker's —
50	   and then calls `mcSetMailboxPassword(mailbox.address, password)` (`:707`). Mailcow keys mailboxes
51	   by **address**, so this sets the password on the victim's real, live mailbox. The new password is
52	   returned to the attacker (`:721`).
53	
54	Cost of the attack: the price of the cheapest email plan. Impact: full read/send access to another
55	customer's business email, plus a denial of service (the victim is locked out). **This must be fixed
56	before any customer is onboarded** — the minimum fix is a global uniqueness check plus `@@unique` on
57	`EmailSubscription.domainName` and `@unique` on `Mailbox.address`, and requiring domain ownership or
58	completed DNS verification before any mailbox operation.
59	
60	### Top 10 gaps, in priority order
61	
62	1. **Stripe confirm/webhook race — customer charged, service never delivered.**
63	   `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:21` credits the wallet on `checkout.session.completed`.
64	   `app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts:27` then gets `credited === false` (P2002 replay guard in
65	   `lib/stripe.ts:242`) and **skips** `placeOrder` (`:32`), `applyResize` (`:54`) and
66	   `applyDiskExpand` (`:78`), falling through to a bare redirect. `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set in
67	   `.env`, so the webhook is live and this race is reachable today. The customer pays, the money
68	   lands in their wallet, the server is never provisioned / the resize never applied / the disk
69	   never grown — **silently, with no error**. Fulfilment must key off its own idempotency record,
70	   not off the wallet-credit flag.
71	
72	2. **SSL issuance is simulated on production and reports success.**
73	   `worker/ssl.ts:303` gates real certbot on `ENABLE_REAL_SSL === "1"`. That variable is **not set
74	   in `/opt/nxeon/.env`** (only `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION` and `ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL` are). Production
75	   therefore falls to `worker/ssl.ts:319-335`, which writes `status: "ACTIVE"`, a fabricated
76	   `expiresAt = now + 90d`, and notifies the customer *"Your Let's Encrypt certificate is active."*
77	   No certificate exists on the box. `components/customer/SslManager.tsx:204` renders that fake
78	   expiry as fact. There is also no renewal sweep (`SslCertificate.autoRenew` is written by
79	   `lib/actions-ssl.ts:121` and read by nothing).
80	
81	3. **Renewals have no card auto-charge — good-card customers get suspended.**
82	   The user asked for this explicitly at 19:06 ("credit cards need to be primary payment method for
83	   auto charged"). `worker/billing.ts:134` debits the wallet only; `:192-214` suspends after grace.
84	   `User.stripeCustomerId` / `stripePaymentMethodId` (`prisma/schema.prisma:135-136`) are **never
85	   written and never read**. No `off_session`, no `SetupIntent`, no `setup_future_usage` anywhere.
86	   Six dunning templates exist (`lib/mailer.ts:340-473`) with exactly **one** call site — the admin
87	   preview page. The engine was scoped and agreed, not built.
88	
89	4. **The migration result card still says "Migration complete 🎉" in green when the migration
90	   left domains dark.** This is the precise bug the 19:46 verification gate was built to kill, and
91	   it survived one layer up. `components/customer/MigrationWizard.tsx:1331` computes `withIssues`,
92	   then `:1332` folds it into `done`, and `:1352` + `:1368-1370` render the emerald progress bar and
93	   the "Migration complete 🎉" card for `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` identically to a clean run. Only the
94	   small `StatusDot` is amber. Separately, the honest per-step summary written to
95	   `Migration.items.results` (`worker/migrate.ts:190`) is **never read by any UI** — the customer
96	   sees only an 8 000-char log tail.
97	
98	5. **Game-server settings apply is simulated on production and claims success with no caveat.**
99	   `worker/game-config.ts:39` requires `ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG === "1"`; it is unset. The simulated
100	   branch (`:76-97`) stamps a marker and notifies *"Game settings applied on `<hostname>` — Minecraft
101	   (vanilla) settings were applied."* — the `(sandbox)` qualifier is appended only when
102	   `NXEON_SANDBOX` is set, which it is not in production. Nothing touches the VM.
103	
104	6. **Volume detach has no safety check, and the confirmation says the opposite.**
105	   `lib/actions-volumes.ts:147-164` guards only on status; `worker/volumes.ts:236` yanks the disk out
106	   of the VM config with no unmount or in-use probe. `components/customer/Volumes.tsx:172` tells the
107	   customer *"Detach … Data is preserved."* — which is false for a volume carrying `/var/lib/docker`,
108	   the exact configuration the migration engine creates (`worker/migrate-real.ts:227`, `:1323-1371`).
109	   Safe-detach was recommended three times in-session and never built. (The *reinstall* guard **was**
110	   built and is real — `worker/index.ts:428-448`.)
111	
112	7. **Backups: a customer's manual backup can delete the platform's own VM backups, and a paid
113	   add-on does nothing.** `lib/proxmox.ts:413-429` prunes by `vmid` across the whole `backup` PVE
114	   storage — the same `/tank/backup` that `scripts/backup-vms.sh:31-35` writes platform backups into.
115	   Separately, the deploy wizard sells **"Daily backups"** (`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:209`),
116	   stores it as `addons.dailyBackup` (`lib/order.ts:183`), and **nothing ever reads it** to set
117	   `Server.autoBackup` (default `false`, `prisma/schema.prisma:342`). A customer who ticks that box
118	   gets no scheduled backups. Pruning also only ever runs on the success path of a *new* backup — no
119	   standalone retention sweep exists.
120	
121	8. **Coupon codes on card top-ups are accepted, promised, and silently ignored.**
122	   `components/customer/CouponField.tsx:60-66` renders *"Code X applied — 20% bonus … Bonus is
123	   credited when you add funds."* and writes an `nxeon_coupon` cookie. That cookie is read in exactly
124	   one place — `lib/actions.ts:527`, inside the **demo** gateway that hard-refuses in production. The
125	   real card top-up (`app/api/stripe/checkout/route.ts:26-42`) has no `discounts`, no
126	   `allow_promotion_codes`, and `creditCheckoutSession` credits `amount_total` verbatim.
127	
128	9. **No email is sent for any billing failure, suspension, or termination.**
129	   `grep -rn "sendMail" worker/*.ts` returns **zero** matches. `worker/billing.ts:205-212` and
130	   `:423-449` write in-app `Notification` rows only. `emails.suspended` and `emails.serverTerminated`
131	   are referenced solely by `app/admin/email-templates/page.tsx`. A customer whose server is
132	   suspended for non-payment gets a bell icon in a portal they are no longer logging into. 29 of the
133	   33 catalog templates have no sender at all.
134	
135	10. **The migration engine's TLS ladder is unreachable in production because the caller drops three
136	    of its inputs.** `worker/migrate.ts:156-167` calls `runRealMigration` with only
137	    `{migration, target, items, report}` — never `cloudflareToken`, `acmeEmail` or `knownDomains`
138	    (declared at `worker/migrate-real.ts:182-184`). Consequences: rung 3 (DNS-01 wildcard via the
139	    customer's connected Cloudflare) can **never** fire even for customers who have connected
140	    (`:2967`, `:2988`); every certificate is issued `--register-unsafely-without-email` (`:2831-2833`)
141	    so no expiry warnings ever arrive; registered `Domain` rows are excluded from the published set.
142	    And `issueMigrationCertificates` (`worker/migrate-real.ts:3097`) — the documented "call again
143	    after DNS moves" entry point — **has zero callers**, so TLS is never retried after cutover.
144	
145	Runners-up, all real but below the line: off-site backups are inert
146	(`scripts/backup-offsite.sh:27-31`, `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env` has no target set); Proxmox
147	`:8006` and host SSH are open to the internet (`scripts/firewall.nft:28,33`); no migration rehearsal
148	harness exists; `ROADMAP.md` is misleading in both directions; tax is configured and never charged.

283	## Contradictions & risks
284	
285	This section matters most. Everything below is a place where the code disagrees with what the user
286	was told, or where something was reported complete and is not.
287	
288	### 1. "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES is terminal, amber in the UI" — the card is green and says "Migration complete 🎉"
289	
290	At 19:48 the user was told the verification gate was *"built and — importantly — **wired end to
291	end**"*, with the assistant specifically calling out that it had caught `worker/migrate.ts`
292	hardcoding `status: "DONE"` and fixed it. That fix is real. But one layer up:
293	
294	```
295	MigrationWizard.tsx:1331   const withIssues = row?.status === "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES";
296	MigrationWizard.tsx:1332   const done = row?.status === "DONE" || withIssues;
297	MigrationWizard.tsx:1352   ... done ? "bg-emerald-400" ...
298	MigrationWizard.tsx:1368   <div className="card border-emerald-500/30">
299	MigrationWizard.tsx:1370     Migration complete 🎉
300	```
301	
302	`withIssues` is computed and then used **only** to widen `done`. A migration that left six domains
303	dark renders an emerald progress bar and a green "Migration complete 🎉" card, identical to a clean
304	run. The only differentiator is a small status dot. This is the same class of bug — value computed
305	correctly, discarded by the caller — that the entire gate was built to eliminate, reproduced in the
306	same commit. And the itemised blockers written to `Migration.items.results` (`worker/migrate.ts:190`)
307	are read by no component at all, so the customer never sees the fix commands.
308	
309	### 2. Two production features silently simulate and report success
310	
311	`ENABLE_REAL_SSL` and `ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG` are **not set** in `/opt/nxeon/.env`. Neither is
312	`NXEON_SANDBOX`. So on production:
313	
314	- **SSL**: `worker/ssl.ts:319-335` marks the certificate `ACTIVE`, invents `expiresAt = now + 90d`,
315	  and notifies *"Your Let's Encrypt certificate is active."* No certbot runs, no certificate exists.
316	  `SslManager.tsx:204` displays the fabricated expiry as fact.
317	- **Game settings**: `worker/game-config.ts:88-96` notifies *"Game settings applied on `<hostname>`"*
318	  with no caveat (the `(sandbox)` suffix is gated on `NXEON_SANDBOX`, which is off). The VM is never
319	  touched.
320	
321	At 10:14 the user was told these flags "default to safe/simulated on prod" and shown a command to
322	enable them — the command covered only `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION` and `ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL`. SSL and
323	game-config were never included in any enable instruction, and the user's 19:04 SSL complaint was
324	answered with a queueing explanation that did not mention the certificate would be fake either way.
325	
326	### 3. Money can be taken without the service being delivered
327	
328	The Stripe confirm route and the Stripe webhook both call `creditCheckoutSession`, and **all
329	fulfilment is gated on that call returning `true`**:
330	
331	```
332	confirm/route.ts:27   const credited = await creditCheckoutSession(sessionId);
333	confirm/route.ts:32   if (credited) { ... placeOrder ... }
334	confirm/route.ts:54   if (credited) { ... applyResize ... }
335	confirm/route.ts:78   if (credited) { ... applyDiskExpand ... }
336	webhook/route.ts:21   await creditCheckoutSession(session.id);   // and nothing else
337	stripe.ts:242         if (P2002) return false;                   // raced — already credited
338	```
339	
340	If the webhook wins the race (Stripe fires it independently of the browser redirect), the customer's
341	card is charged, the wallet is credited, and the deploy / resize / disk expansion **never happens**.
342	The redirect lands on a bare server list with no error. `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is populated, so this
343	is live. The in-code comments assert the opposite ("provisioning runs exactly once even if the
344	confirm URL is reloaded") — true for reloads, false for webhook-first ordering.
345	
346	### 4. Three customer-facing promises the code does not keep
347	
348	| Promise shown to the customer | Reality |
349	|---|---|
350	| `CouponField.tsx:60-66` — "Code applied — 20% bonus · Bonus is credited when you add funds" | The cookie is read only by the demo gateway (`lib/actions.ts:527`), which refuses in production. `app/api/stripe/checkout/route.ts` applies no discount. No bonus, no error |
351	| `Volumes.tsx:172` — "Detach … Data is preserved." | No unmount, no in-use check (`worker/volumes.ts:236`). For a volume holding `/var/lib/docker` — which is exactly what the migration engine puts there — this destroys the server's Docker state |
352	| `MailSettings.tsx:234` — display name "Shown as the sender name on messages you send" | `lib/actions-mail.ts:431` sends `from: cred.address` with no display name and no `Reply-To`. The field is saved and never used |
353	
354	Add the **"Daily backups" add-on** (`DeployWizard.tsx:209` → `lib/order.ts:183` → read by nothing),
355	and the WHOIS-privacy checklist item that ticks green off a DB flag no registrar ever saw
356	(`lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:133-151` vs `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:115`).
357	
358	### 5. A customer's backup button can delete the platform's backups
359	
360	`lib/proxmox.ts:413-429` prunes by `vmid` across the whole `backup` PVE storage — which resolves to
361	`/tank/backup`, the same directory `scripts/backup-vms.sh:31-35` writes host-level platform backups
362	into. A customer clicking "Create backup" prunes *all* archives for that VMID down to 2, platform
363	copies included. Currently masked because the production drop-in also forces `keep-last=2`, but the
364	two retention policies are meant to differ (the user asked for system=3, customer=2) and the moment
365	they do, the customer's action wins.
366	
367	### 6. "Backup failed — your server is unaffected" is shown for restores, where it is false
368	
369	`BackupControls.tsx:130-150` is shared between backup and restore. For a restore it renders
370	*"Restore failed — your server is unaffected · No changes were made to your running server."*
371	But `BACKUP_RESTORE` is in `VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS` (`worker/index.ts:50`), and by the time it fails
372	`worker/restore.ts:103-110` has already stopped the VM and begun overwriting its disk. The most
373	reassuring message in the product appears in its most destructive failure case.
374	
375	### 7. `ROADMAP.md` is the file the user reaches for, and it is wrong in both directions
376	
377	Last updated 2026-07-24 03:50. It marks **"Subscription/billing engine (renewals, grace, suspend,
378	dunning/termination)"** as `[x]` at line 124 — there is no dunning engine and no card charging. It
379	simultaneously lists as *unchecked* five things that have shipped (root-password encryption `:61`,
380	standalone build `:62` — correctly unchecked, non-root web `:64`, SMTP credentials `:80`, 2FA at
381	login `:84`). The assistant offered at 18:31 to "reconcile ROADMAP.md to reality first so it's
382	trustworthy" as option (b); the user chose (a) and it was never revisited. The user then asked "what
383	else needs to be done" five more times.
384	
385	### 8. Volumes are marketed and modelled as portable; they are not
386	
387	The whole 17:42–18:05 design discussion concluded on "volumes stay portable — your data survives a
388	server rebuild and can move between servers," and that framing is in the docs and the UI. In code:
389	
390	- `lib/actions-volumes.ts:129-131` refuses to attach a volume to any server other than the one
391	  recorded in `volume.serverId`;
392	- `worker/volumes.ts:240` never clears `serverId` on detach.
393	
394	A volume is therefore pinned to its first server for life. Nothing formats or mounts it either — the
395	attach notification (`worker/volumes.ts:204`) tells the customer to do that themselves, so "one
396	volume, one filesystem, mounted at a data path" exists only inside the migration engine
397	(`worker/migrate-real.ts:227`, `:1300`).

399	### 9. The engine's best TLS work is unreachable because the caller drops its arguments
400	
401	`worker/migrate-real.ts` declares `cloudflareToken`, `acmeEmail` and `knownDomains` (`:182-184`) and
402	implements a complete three-rung TLS ladder around them. `worker/migrate.ts:156-167` passes none of
403	them. Result: DNS-01 wildcard issuance can never fire (`:2967`, `:2988`) even for a customer who has
404	completed the Cloudflare OAuth flow the user specifically asked for; every certificate is issued
405	without a registration email so no expiry warnings will ever arrive; and `issueMigrationCertificates`
406	(`:3097`), the documented post-cutover re-issue entry point, has **zero callers**. The user was told
407	at 16:19 that the "3-layer TLS ladder" shipped.
408	
409	### 10. Stale documentation that now contradicts the code it describes
410	
411	- `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md:136-143` still states the migration status is hardcoded. That was
412	  fixed in `8e93b13`. The document's own thesis is that unread field notes are worthless.
413	- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md:1210` documents the Cloudflare scope default that Cloudflare rejects.
414	- `lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts:159-165`'s comment claims scope should be sent only if an operator opts
415	  in — the non-empty default at `:59` means it is always sent.
416	- Commit `8c8b7d9`'s message claims the resize-shrink fix; `git blame` puts that fix in `29ea0d3`,
417	  and `8c8b7d9` does not touch `worker/index.ts` at all.
418	
419	### 11. Process risks the session itself created
420	
421	Stated plainly because they shape the launch decision:
422	
423	- The **double-count bug** shipped at ~16:00 caused the user to buy ~40 GB of **one-way,
424	  unrefundable** disk (~$4/mo, unrecoverable without rebuilding the server). No test asserts that the
425	  wizard's sizing and the engine's sizing agree — the class of bug can recur tomorrow.
426	- The worker was **restarted mid-migration**, killing the user's first attempt, in violation of a
427	  freeze rule stated minutes earlier.
428	- A deploy was reported "closed out cleanly" while the agent was still writing files; the follow-up
429	  build caught a **latent hard-failure in plan resize** for any customer holding purchased extra
430	  disk. That bug reached production briefly and was found by luck, not by a check.
431	- **No CI, no pre-deploy gate.** `npm run check` exists; nothing enforces it.
432	
433	### 12. Background agents are still writing into the live production tree, right now
434	
435	While this audit ran, files changed under me in `/opt/nxeon` that no part of this audit touched:
436	
437	| File | Modified | Origin |
438	|---|---|---|
439	| `lib/markdown.ts` | 19:59:32 | in-flight docs-renderer change |
440	| `docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md` | 20:16:45 | QA audit agent (new file) |
441	| `components/customer/CloudflareConnect.tsx` | 20:17:19 | adds an inline `CloudflareMark` SVG to the Connect button |
442	
443	These are the agents the assistant launched at 19:58 and never integrated — the session ended first.
444	So the working tree currently contains **uncommitted, undeployed, unreviewed changes to a production
445	component**, and `HEAD` no longer describes what is on disk. This is the same concurrent-write hazard
446	the assistant diagnosed at 04:07 ("a background agent runs `npm run build` on the same `/opt/nxeon`
447	tree while I'm also building… corrupts the output") and solved with a no-build rule for agents — the
448	rule stops build races but does nothing about agents mutating shared source between a review and a
449	deploy. Whoever deploys next will ship these three files without having read them.
450	
451	`docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md` is worth reading in full: it is where the email-takeover vulnerability at the
452	top of this document came from.

457	- Current live DNS for `nxeon.cloud` (SPF/DMARC/PTR): outbound DNS resolution is unavailable from

# Nxeon — the internal manual

The single reference for how this platform actually works: what each feature does, which file does
it, how it fails, and how you diagnose it at 3am. Rendered privately at **`/admin/docs`**.

**Read this first.** Three rules govern the whole document:

1. **Reference leads, history follows.** Parts I–VII are reference. The dated change log is Part
   VIII, at the bottom, kept verbatim.
2. **Every `file:line` was opened and read.** Line numbers drift as several agents edit this tree
   concurrently — treat them as "this function, roughly here", and grep the quoted symbol if a
   number has slipped.
3. **This manual does not overclaim.** The single recurring defect in this codebase is *a surface
   reporting an outcome it never verified*. A manual that asserted features work because the code
   looks complete would be the same bug in a new place. Where something is simulated, partial, or
   saved-and-never-read, the chapter says so and **Known gaps — the honest inventory** lists it.

Companion documents you should not edit but should read:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `docs/AUDIT-24H.md` | Line-by-line verification of a 24h session. The "top 10 gaps" list is the best map of trust debt in this repo. |
| `docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md` | Pre-launch QA sweep. Source of the cross-tenant email-takeover finding. |
| `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` | 28 numbered real migration failures with fixes. Acceptance criteria for the migration engine. |
| `docs/MIGRATION.md` | Moving the Nxeon *platform itself* to another box (not customer migration). |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Agent-facing conventions and safety rules. |
| `ROADMAP.md` | Historically unreliable in both directions — see Known gaps. |

---

## What Nxeon is

Nxeon is a self-hosted, Hostinger-style VPS hosting business. A visitor lands on the marketing
site, picks a plan and a term, pays, and about ninety seconds later has a root shell on a real
KVM virtual machine — plus, from the same portal, domains, TLS, mailboxes, block storage, backups,
game servers, a web console, an AI build assistant, and a one-click lift-and-shift migration from
whatever host they are leaving.

It runs on **one** dedicated server. Everything below is on the same box:

- **Hypervisor**: Proxmox VE 9 on an OVH KS-GAME (i7-7700K, 64 GB RAM). Storage is a 2×450 GB NVMe
  ZFS mirror (`data`, 358 G) for VM disks and a 4 TB HDD pool (`tank`, 3.6 T) for backups.
- **Guests**: customer VMs cloned from cloud-init templates VMID 9000–9009, plus VMID **8000
  `nxeon-mail`** — the Mailcow appliance that carries every mailbox on the platform, both the
  transactional sender and paid customer business email.
- **Web + worker + Postgres**: on the Proxmox host itself, not in a VM.

Product surface, in one place:

```
 MARKETING (app/(marketing))          CUSTOMER PORTAL (app/dashboard)      ADMIN (app/admin)
 ─────────────────────────────        ──────────────────────────────       ─────────────────
 /  pricing  vps  domains             servers   deploy    migrate          servers   users
 game-servers  business-email         volumes   ssl       domains          plans     products
 block-storage  migrate               mail      calendar  email           invoices  billing
 vibe-coding  compare  blog           games     build     claude-code      jobs      nodes  ips
 tools/* (12 free tools)              billing   invoices  team             domains   mail
 legal/*  status  help                support   settings  refer            support   abuse
                                      projects  activity  feedback         docs      settings
```

Three properties are worth internalising before you touch anything:

- **Nothing mutates a VM from the web tier.** Every state change is a `Job` row that the worker
  picks up. The web app may *read* Proxmox freely; it may not write. This is why "I clicked the
  button and nothing happened" is almost always a worker question, not a web question.
- **One in-flight job per server.** Enforced in the server-action layer, and the worker itself is a
  strictly serial single-job queue. A 24-minute migration blocks every other customer's SSL
  issuance behind it. That is a known, unfixed design limit — see Known gaps.
- **Money is integer cents, everywhere.** `balanceCents`, `priceCents`, `amountCents`. There are no
  floats in the billing path.

## Architecture at a glance

```
                                 INTERNET
                                     │
     :80 :443 ───────────────────────┼─────────────── :25 :465 :587 :993 :4190
        │                            │                          │
   ┌────▼─────────────────────────────────────────┐              │
   │  nginx  (host)                                │             │  DNAT
   │  /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/                    │             │  scripts/mail-nat.sh
   │    nxeon-cloud        → customer portal :3000 │             │
   │    nxeon-admin-cloud  → admin portal    :3000 │             │
   │    nxeon-staging      → staging         :3001 │             │
   │    nxeon-mail         → Mailcow UI            │             │
   │  generated by scripts/configure-domains.sh    │             │
   │  from /etc/nxeon/domains.env  (never by hand) │             │
   └────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────────┘             │
        │                      │                                 │
        │ HTTP                 │ WebSocket                        │
        │                      │                                 │
 ┌──────▼───────────────┐  ┌───▼────────────────────┐   ┌────────▼─────────────────┐
 │ nxeon-web.service    │  │ nxeon-terminal.service │   │ VM 8000  nxeon-mail      │
 │ Next.js 15 App Router│  │  PTY  → xterm.js       │   │ Mailcow: postfix,        │
 │ User=nxeon, :3000    │  │ nxeon-console-proxy    │   │ dovecot, rspamd, SOGo    │
 │ server actions       │  │  VNC   → noVNC         │   │ REST API MAILCOW_API_URL │
 └──────┬───────────────┘  └───┬────────────────────┘   └────────▲─────────────────┘
        │ Prisma                │ ssh/vnc                         │ lib/mailcow.ts
        │                       │                                 │ lib/mailer.ts (SMTP)
 ┌──────▼────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
 │ PostgreSQL 17    db "nxeon"  /  db "nxeon_staging"     │◄───────┘
 │ prisma/schema.prisma — 60 models, Job is the spine    │
 └──────▲──────────────────────────────┬─────────────────┘
        │ Prisma                        │ polls Job every 3s
        │                        ┌──────▼─────────────────────────────┐
        │                        │ nxeon-worker.service  (User=root)  │
        │                        │ worker/index.ts — serial job loop  │
        │                        │  + sweeps: billing 10m, products   │
        │                        │    10m, backups 15m, monitor 10m,  │
        │                        │    abuse 10m, geo 90s, games 6h    │
        │                        └──────┬─────────────────────────────┘
        │                               │ Proxmox API + ssh + iptables
        │                        ┌──────▼─────────────────────────────┐
        │                        │ Proxmox VE 9   (same host)         │
        │                        │ pvedaemon :8006, token nxeon@pve   │
        │                        │ lib/proxmox.ts is the ONLY client  │
        │                        └──────┬─────────────────────────────┘
        │                               │ qm clone / config / resize
        │        ┌──────────────────────▼──────────────────────────┐
        │        │ Customer VMs — bridge vmbr1, NAT 10.20.0.0/24   │
        │        │ IPs .100–.250 (prod) / .50–.99 (staging)        │
        │        │ SSH via DNAT 20000–29999 in iptables NXEON_FWD  │
        │        │ rebuilt from the DB by worker/network.ts        │
        │        └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
 ┌──────▼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ ZFS   data (358G, NVMe mirror) → vmdata : live VM disks          │
 │       tank (3.6T, HDD)         → /tank/backup/dump    customer   │
 │                                → /tank/backup/platform  platform │
 │                                → /tank/backup/snippets cloud-init│
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Ownership boundaries that matter:

| Concern | Sole owner | Never do this instead |
|---|---|---|
| Proxmox mutations | `lib/proxmox.ts`, called from `worker/` | Call the PVE API from a server action |
| VM IP / SSH port allocation | `lib/ipam.ts` | Pick a free IP by hand |
| iptables DNAT | `worker/network.ts`, chain `NXEON_FWD` | Edit the chain manually — it is rebuilt from the DB |
| nginx vhosts for the platform | `scripts/configure-domains.sh` | Hand-edit `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/*` |
| The domain name | `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` | Hardcode a hostname in app code |
| Mailcow | `lib/mailcow.ts` | Click around the Mailcow UI for anything scripted |

## Request lifecycle — browser to Proxmox

Two paths. Reads go straight through; writes detour through the `Job` table.

```
READ PATH — "show me my server"
 browser
   │ GET /dashboard/servers/abc
   ▼
 nginx :443 ──► nxeon-web :3000
   │
   ├─ middleware / layout: currentUser() from signed cookie   lib/auth.ts
   │     └─ impersonation: currentUser() = target, realUser() = the admin
   ├─ RSC page: db.server.findUnique(...)                     Prisma → Postgres
   ├─ live status/metrics: vmStatus() / RRD via /api/metrics  lib/proxmox.ts (READ ok)
   ▼
 HTML streamed back


WRITE PATH — "reboot my server"
 browser
   │ server action  (POST, RSC)
   ▼
 nxeon-web
   ├─ 1. requireUser() / requireAdmin() / requireArea()       lib/rbac.ts, lib/auth.ts
   ├─ 2. ownership check: server.userId === user.id
   ├─ 3. impersonation spend-guard for money actions
   ├─ 4. one-in-flight guard: any Job for this server QUEUED|RUNNING → refuse
   ├─ 5. db.job.create({ type: "REBOOT", serverId, payload })
   └─ 6. revalidatePath() → UI shows the job as pending
        (the action returns HERE. Nothing has touched Proxmox yet.)
                       │
                       │  ≤3s later
                       ▼
 nxeon-worker  poll ──► atomic claim ──► handler ──► Proxmox ──► DB update
                                                        └─ Notification row
```

Step 4 is the single most common source of "the button does nothing": a previous job stuck in
`RUNNING` blocks every subsequent action on that server. `reapStuckJobs()`
(`/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:1008`) clears those on worker start, which is why a worker restart
often "fixes" a wedged server — and why restarting during a live job is dangerous.

## Job lifecycle — the worker queue

`worker/index.ts` is one `for(;;)` loop. It does housekeeping sweeps on timers, then tries to claim
exactly one job, runs it to completion, and loops.

```
                       ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
   server action  ────►│ Job { status: QUEUED, attempts: 0 }     │
                       └───────────────┬─────────────────────────┘
                                       │
  worker/index.ts:1136  findFirst({ status: QUEUED }, orderBy createdAt asc )
                                       │
  :1144  ATOMIC CLAIM
         updateMany({ where: { id, status: QUEUED },
                      data: { status: RUNNING, attempts: +1 } })
         claim.count === 1 ? mine : someone else took it, re-poll
                                       │
                                       ▼
  :771   handlers[job.type]      ── 35 JobTypes, one function each
                                       │
              ┌────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┐
              │ success                │ throw                  │
              ▼                        ▼                        │
     status: DONE            attempts < MAX_ATTEMPTS(3)?        │
     progress: 100            ├─ yes → back to QUEUED ──────────┘  (retry)
     Notification             └─ no  → status: FAILED
                                        ├─ reconcileFailedJob()  refunds money
                                        └─ if type ∈ VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS
                                              server.status = ERROR
```

`VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS` (`/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:49`) is the list of job types whose failure
genuinely leaves the VM in a bad run/disk state, and therefore the only ones that may mark the
server `ERROR`:

```
PROVISION  REINSTALL  DELETE  RESIZE  START  STOP  REBOOT  SUSPEND
UNSUSPEND  BACKUP_RESTORE  SNAPSHOT_ROLLBACK
```

Two deliberate absences, both bug fixes:

- **`BACKUP_CREATE` is absent** because backups run in `mode: "snapshot"` and never stop the VM.
  A customer once reported "I tried creating a backup but it just shut down the server"; the fix
  was to stop treating a failed backup as a VM-state failure.
- **`DISK_EXPAND` is absent** because growing a disk cannot change the run state. Its money is
  unwound by `reconcileFailedJob` instead. Comment at `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:44`.

The full job type list, grouped:

| Group | Job types |
|---|---|
| Lifecycle | `PROVISION` `START` `STOP` `REBOOT` `REINSTALL` `DELETE` `PASSWORD_RESET` |
| Billing-driven | `SUSPEND` `UNSUSPEND` |
| Capacity | `RESIZE` `DISK_EXPAND` |
| Data protection | `SNAPSHOT_CREATE` `SNAPSHOT_DELETE` `SNAPSHOT_ROLLBACK` `BACKUP_CREATE` `BACKUP_RESTORE` |
| Volumes | `VOLUME_CREATE` `VOLUME_ATTACH` `VOLUME_DETACH` `VOLUME_DELETE` |
| Control panel | `WEBSITE_CREATE` `WEBSITE_DELETE` `WEBSITE_TOGGLE` `WEBSITE_SSL` `DB_CREATE` `DB_DELETE` `APP_INSTALL` `CRON_SYNC` `SERVICE_ACTION` |
| Other subsystems | `SSL_ISSUE` `MIGRATE` `GAME_CONFIG` `GAME_UPDATE` `CLAUDE_BUILD` `SYNC_FORWARDS` |

Sweeps, all registered inline in `main()` at `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:1029`:

| Sweep | Interval | Function | File |
|---|---|---|---|
| Renewals + dunning | 10 min | `billingSweep()` | `worker/billing.ts` |
| Add-on product renewals | 10 min | `productRenewalSweep()` | `worker/product-renewals.ts` |
| Scheduled customer backups | 15 min | `scheduledBackupSweep()` | `worker/backup-schedule.ts` |
| Monitoring alerts | 10 min | `monitorSweep()` | `worker/monitor.ts` |
| In-guest disk sampling | 10 min | `sampleServerDisks()` | `worker/monitor.ts` |
| Abuse detection | 10 min | `abuseSweep()` | `worker/abuse.ts` |
| Visit geo-enrichment | 90 s | `geoEnrichSweep()` | `worker/geo.ts` |
| Game auto-update | 6 h | `gameUpdateSweep()` | `worker/game-update.ts` |
| Dedicated-IP pool import | 5 min | `syncDedicatedIpPool()` | `lib/dedicated-ip.ts` |

Every sweep is individually `try`/`catch`ed with a `console.error`, so one failing sweep cannot stop
the loop — but it also means a permanently broken sweep is invisible except in the journal. Grep for
`sweep error` when something scheduled has quietly stopped happening.

## Environments — production, staging, and the .env contract

The code is byte-identical between environments. Every difference is an environment variable. That
is the whole isolation model, so a wrong value in `.env` is how staging would eat production's IP
pool.

| | Production | Staging |
|---|---|---|
| Tree | `/opt/nxeon` | `/opt/nxeon-staging` |
| Database | `nxeon` | `nxeon_staging` |
| Web service | `nxeon-web.service` :3000 | `nxeon-staging-web.service` :3001 |
| Worker | `nxeon-worker.service` | `nxeon-staging-worker.service` |
| Terminal backend | `nxeon-terminal.service` | `nxeon-terminal-staging.service` |
| Console proxy | `nxeon-console-proxy.service` | `nxeon-staging-console-proxy.service` |
| VM IP pool | `10.20.0.100–250` | `10.20.0.50–99` |
| SSH DNAT ports | `20000–29999` | `30000–30999` |
| iptables chain | `NXEON_FWD` | `NXEON_FWD_STG` |
| Proxmox VM tag | *(none)* | `nxeon-staging` |
| Admin credentials | `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt` | `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt` |

The variables that create the split: `NXEON_ENV`, `NXEON_COOKIE_NAME`, `NXEON_NAT_CHAIN`,
`NXEON_TAG`, `NXEON_IP_START`, `NXEON_IP_END`, `NXEON_SSH_PORT_START`, `NXEON_SSH_PORT_END`,
`NXEON_CRED_FILE`, `PORT`, `APP_URL`.

**They share one Proxmox node and one ZFS pool.** Nothing but those ranges keeps them apart. Never
point staging pools at production ranges; never `qm destroy` anything with a `Server` row.

Deploy flow:

```
  edit /opt/nxeon  ──► git commit ──► post-commit hook auto-pushes to GitHub
                                         │
                       scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]
                                         │  build + prisma db push + restart staging
                                         ▼
                            verify on STAGING_HOST / :8080
                                         │
                       scripts/promote-production.sh
                                         │  rebuild + restart production
                                         ▼
                                     live
```

Domains and TLS are driven from **`/etc/nxeon/domains.env`** — currently
`BASE_DOMAIN=nxeon.cloud`, `ADMIN_HOST=4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.revsports.ca` (deliberately an unguessable
subdomain; `/admin` 404s on the customer host), `STAGING_HOST=staging.revsports.ca`. To move the
platform to a new domain: edit those four values, point DNS at the box, run
`scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates every vhost, obtains Let's Encrypt certificates,
rewrites `APP_URL` in both `.env` files, and restarts web. That is the entire migration.

## Codebase map

```
/opt/nxeon
├── app/
│   ├── (marketing)/       public site: pricing, product pages, 12 free tools, legal, blog
│   ├── dashboard/         customer portal — one dir per feature
│   ├── admin/             ops portal — 40+ sections incl. /admin/docs (this page)
│   └── api/               route handlers: stripe, metrics, console, files, mail,
│                          terminal token, tools, v1 (API tokens), health, search
├── components/
│   ├── ui/primitives.tsx  the design system: Card, Badge, StatusDot, PageHeader…
│   ├── ui/charts.tsx      dependency-free SVG charts — do not add a chart library
│   ├── portal/Shell.tsx   the shared sidebar shell for BOTH portals
│   ├── customer/          feature components (DeployWizard, MigrationWizard, mail/*…)
│   ├── admin/             admin panels
│   └── marketing/         hero, marquee, animated product showcases
├── lib/
│   ├── actions*.ts        server actions, one file per domain  ("use server")
│   ├── proxmox.ts         the only Proxmox client
│   ├── ipam.ts            IP + SSH port allocation
│   ├── proration.ts       THE shared money-per-day function
│   ├── stripe*.ts         checkout, cards-on-file
│   ├── mailcow.ts mailer.ts mail/*  email in and out
│   ├── registrar.ts       name.com / Namecheap domain APIs
│   ├── cloudflare-*.ts    OAuth + DNS writes
│   ├── markdown.ts        the renderer this document is displayed with
│   └── rbac.ts settings.ts crypto-box.ts …
├── worker/
│   ├── index.ts           the loop + most handlers
│   ├── billing.ts         renewals, card auto-charge, dunning, suspend, terminate
│   ├── migrate-real.ts    5.3k lines — the real lift-and-shift engine
│   ├── migrate-detect.ts  read-only source-server survey
│   ├── migrate.ts         the MIGRATE job wrapper that calls one of the above
│   ├── volumes.ts ssl.ts disk-expand.ts game-config.ts restore.ts …
├── prisma/schema.prisma   60 models
├── scripts/               ops shell + tsx: backups, domains, firewall, e2e, nightly scan
├── deploy/                systemd units + timers, kept in git
├── terminal-server/       standalone PTY websocket backend
└── docs/                  this manual + the audits
```

Naming convention worth knowing: **`lib/actions-*.ts` files are `"use server"`**. Everything they
export becomes a POST endpoint. That has bitten this codebase twice — see
**Two-factor authentication** for the brute-force oracle it created, and the E352 files-tab error
caused by exporting a non-async value from one.
