  it is tested. This is the recurring defect in its purest form: a *verification claim* that was
  never verified.
- **`docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md:136-143` is stale.** It says `worker/migrate.ts` "sets
  `status: "DONE"` unconditionally" and that wiring the outcome through is "a one-line change that has
  not been made." It **has** been made (`worker/migrate.ts:412`). The same stale claim is repeated
  inside the engine at `migrate-real.ts:5251`. That document's own thesis is that unread field notes
  are worthless; this is the mirror case — a fixed note nobody updated.
- **`prisma/schema.prisma:1009` lists four statuses; the code writes five.** The comment says
  `PENDING | RUNNING | DONE | FAILED`; `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` is missing from it.
- **There is no rehearsal harness.** No migration test exists. Every bug so far was found by a real
  migration onto a real customer domain. The next customer migration is the gate's first real test.

## Server migration — cutover, re-runs and the missing TLS retry

**DNS repointing is manual, customer-initiated, one click per hostname.** The engine never touches
DNS.

```
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │  Point your domains at the new server                               │
 ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │  studionexis.com        registered with Nxeon    → 51.79.162.96     │
 │                                                     [ Point now ]   │
 │  content.example.ca     found on the new server     [ Point now ]   │
 │  stg.example.com        from the old server's vhosts  ✗ NOT SERVING │
 │                         do not move DNS for this name yet           │
 │                                                                     │
 │  Or roll back: point the A record at your old server.               │
 │  [ Open Cloudflare DNS ↗ ]                                          │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Candidates come from three sources — `getMigrationDnsInfo()` at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-migrate.ts:743`:
`Domain` rows registered with Nxeon (`:764`), `Website` rows on the target (`:772`), and hostnames
inferred from the **stored** scan snapshot's web-root folder names (`:779`). It explicitly never
re-scans the source (`:741`).

The write is `pointMigrationDns()` at `:804` → `pointHostnameToIp` (`lib/cloudflare-point.ts:97`).
Cloudflare only. A **single DNS-only A record**, `proxied: false` — which is load-bearing: an orange-
clouded record breaks HTTP-01 validation, and HTTP-01 is the only challenge the SSL subsystem uses
(`lib/cloudflare-point.ts:12-17`, `:158-162`).

**Cloudflare is involved three ways:** the A-record write above; **DNS-01 wildcard issuance** — a
`*.domain` certificate cannot be issued any other way, so `resolveTlsInputs()`
(`worker/migrate.ts:186`) resolves the customer's token and passes it as `cloudflareToken` (`:389`) to
`secureSites` rung 3 (`migrate-real.ts:3125`) → `issueDns01` (`:2991`); and a deep link for manual
rollback (`MigrationWizard.tsx:1596`).

**How an admin re-runs a failed migration: there is no re-run path.** Verified:

- No admin UI. `db.migration` is referenced only in `lib/actions-migrate.ts`; there is no
  `app/admin/**` migration page at all.
- No retry action. The exported actions are `createMigration` (`:324`), `scanSource` (`:461`),
  `targetDiskFree` (`:575`), `listMigrations` (`:675`), `getMigration` (`:694`),
  `getMigrationDnsInfo` (`:743`), `pointMigrationDns` (`:804`). None re-enqueues.
- No CLI. `scripts/migrate-*.sh` are for moving the platform, not a customer.
- The worker will not retry either: the handler swallows the error (`worker/migrate.ts:562`), so the
  `Job` completes and `MAX_ATTEMPTS` never engages.
- **The secrets are already gone.** `clearSecrets` runs on failure (`migrate.ts:555`), so a bare
  re-enqueue of the same `migrationId` fails at `migrate-real.ts:3318` with *"source SSH password is
  missing or could not be decrypted."*

**The only supported route is to start a new migration** — `MigrationWizard.tsx:1436` ("← Start
another migration") → `createMigration` with freshly entered credentials, rate-limited to 5 per 10
minutes (`lib/actions-migrate.ts:331`). Re-runs are safe by construction: user/group creation
(`:3721`), volume create (`:3781`), `ensureImage`'s present-check (`:1417`) and the
Docker-already-on-its-own-FS pre-flight allowance (`:3472`) are all idempotent.

**The one thing you *can* re-enqueue by hand** is the TLS pass:

```
db.job.create({ data: { type: "MIGRATE", payload: { migrationId, phase: "tls" } } })
```

Documented at `worker/migrate.ts:257`, idempotent via certbot `--keep-until-expiring` (`:251`), copies
nothing (`:245`), and deliberately does **not** touch `Migration.status` (`:252`).

**Honest note — the post-cutover TLS retry has zero callers.** `runPostCutoverTls`
(`worker/migrate.ts:260`) is reached only when `payload.phase === "tls"` (`:341`), and the enqueue
line exists **only inside a comment** (`:258`). A repo-wide grep for `phase: "tls"` returns that
comment and nothing else. `pointMigrationDns` does not enqueue it. So certificates that could not be
issued at migration time — because DNS had not moved yet, which is the normal case — are **never
retried automatically**. `issueMigrationCertificates` (`migrate-real.ts:3236`) exists precisely to
close this, and its own docblock at `migrate.ts:241` says it "had ZERO callers." It still effectively
does. Today, closing the loop means an admin queueing the job above by hand.

**Simulation mode is a live regression risk.** `worker/migrate.ts:20`:

```
const REAL_MIGRATION = process.env.ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION === "1" && !SANDBOX;
```

`ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION=1` is set in `/opt/nxeon/.env:35`, so the real engine runs today. But unlike
`worker/ssl.ts` and `worker/game-config.ts`, which now **throw** outside sandbox when their flag is
off, `worker/migrate.ts:453` falls through to a fully synthetic branch that fabricates step results
("installed", "docker compose up -d succeeded", "engine is active on the target", `:481-523`), writes

                     (ENABLE_REAL_SSL is not set), so no certificate was
                     requested from Let's Encrypt. Nothing was installed —
                     this certificate is NOT active."
```

**The invented-expiry bug is fixed.** It used to be that with the flag unset the worker wrote
`status: "ACTIVE"` with a fabricated `expiresAt = now + 90d` and notified *"Your Let's Encrypt
certificate is active"* — with no certificate anywhere on the box. Two changes closed it: the
fall-through now **throws** (`worker/ssl.ts:692`), and the expiry is the **observed** `notAfter` read
off disk, with a throw if it cannot be parsed (`:311`). The customer UI labels the column
*"Expires (observed)"* (`components/customer/SslCertificates.tsx:424`). `ENABLE_REAL_SSL=1` is set in
`/opt/nxeon/.env:40`, so the real path runs today.

The fabricated 90-day expiry still exists at `worker/ssl.ts:700-717` but is reachable **only** when
`SANDBOX === true` (`NXEON_SANDBOX=1`), and it self-labels the notification `(sandbox)`.

**Challenge type is HTTP-01 via `--standalone`.** certbot spins up its own responder on port 80. There
is no `--webroot` and no DNS-01 in this subsystem (DNS-01 exists only inside the migration engine).
This is why Cloudflare A records written by the platform are always `proxied: false`.

**A successful issue does not mean a served certificate.** `--standalone` does not install into
nginx/apache. That is surfaced as `lastError = notServedWarning` (`worker/ssl.ts:544`, set at `:658`)
rather than as a status change — deliberately, so the row still reflects that a real certificate
exists.

**Data model.** `SslCertificate` (`prisma/schema.prisma:982`): `domain`, `status`
(`PENDING|ISSUING|ACTIVE|FAILED|EXPIRED`), `issuedAt`, `expiresAt`, `autoRenew`, `lastError`,
`serverId`.

**Failure modes.**

| Symptom | Cause | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Stuck `PENDING` for many minutes | The worker is strictly serial and a long job (migration, backup) is ahead | Queue position resolved at `app/dashboard/ssl/page.tsx:44-80` |
| `certbot failed: … Invalid response … 404` | DNS does not point here yet, or Cloudflare proxy is on | Turn the orange cloud off; re-request |
| `port 80 in use` | Something else is bound | The pre-flight at `worker/ssl.ts:407` names it |
| Renewal failed but the cert is still valid | Deliberate: status stays `ACTIVE` | `:729-737` |

**Honest note — nothing renews. `sslSweep` is dead code.** `/opt/nxeon/worker/ssl.ts` contains three
fully written sweeps: `sslReconcileSweep` (`:836`, ages out stranded `PENDING`/`ISSUING` rows and
flips lapsed `ACTIVE` → `EXPIRED`), `sslRenewalSweep` (`:929`, 21-day lead, verifies served state
first, honours `autoRenew`, LE rate caps, backoff ladder, one-job-per-server), and the `sslSweep`
wrapper (`:1058`). **None of them is called.** `worker/index.ts:18` imports only `sslIssue`, and `:795`
wires only `SSL_ISSUE`. A repo-wide grep for `sslSweep|sslRenewalSweep|sslReconcileSweep` matches the
definitions and the *instructions to wire them* in the file's own header (`worker/ssl.ts:11-20`).

So in production today: **no renewal, no expiry reconciliation, no `EXPIRED` transition, and no
cleanup of stranded rows.** Certificates issued now will lapse at 90 days with no warning. Wiring it
is one import and one timer block in `worker/index.ts`, alongside the seven sweeps already there.
`SslCertificate.autoRenew` is written by `lib/actions-ssl.ts:336` and, until that sweep runs, read by
nothing.

## Nxeon Mail — the native webmail client

**What it does.** A full IMAP/SMTP webmail client built into the customer portal, themed to match the
rest of the product. It replaced SOGo's own UI. Plus a CalDAV calendar and tasks view.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ alice@example.com ▾ │  Inbox  🔍 [               ]        [ ✎ Compose ]      │
├──────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┤
│ 📥 Inbox  12 │ ● Stripe        Payment recei… │  Payment receipt — INV-00042  │
│ 📤 Sent      │   2026-07-24 14:02            │  Stripe <no-reply@stripe.com>  │
│ 📝 Drafts    │ ○ Nick          Re: migration │  to me · 2026-07-24 14:02      │
│ 🗑 Trash     │   2026-07-24 11:40   📎2      │  ───────────────────────────   │
│ 🚫 Junk      │ ○ Cloudflare    Zone updated  │  Your payment of $195.58 has   │
│ 📁 Archive   │   2026-07-23 09:15            │  been received…                │
│              │                               │                                │
│              │            ▲ 50/page          │  📎 invoice.pdf   📎 logo.png  │
│              │                               │  [Reply] [Fwd] [Move ▾] [🗑]   │
└──────────────┴───────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┘
```

The mail and calendar routes render **full-bleed** — `components/portal/Shell.tsx:225` sets
`fullBleed` for them and `:507` swaps the padded main for `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-hidden`.

**Transport.** `/opt/nxeon/lib/mail/types.ts:8-11` — `MAIL_IMAP_HOST` defaults to `10.20.0.10` port
993, `MAIL_SMTP_HOST` the same host port 587. Neither variable is set in `.env`, so **those literals
are live**: the client talks to the Mailcow VM over the NAT bridge by IP, while sending the correct
TLS SNI (`MAIL_TLS_SERVERNAME`, default `mail.nxeon.cloud`, `lib/mail/imap.ts:70`) and **not**
verifying the certificate (`rejectUnauthorized: false`, `:309`). Same shape for SMTP
(`lib/actions-mail.ts:490-497`). Connections are per-request and always closed — `withImap` (`:320`),
`withMailbox` (`:342`).

**Credentials.** `Mailbox.passwordEnc` (`prisma/schema.prisma:675`), AES-256-GCM via
`lib/crypto-box.ts:22` with a key derived by `scryptSync(AUTH_SECRET, "nxeon-byok", 32)`. Every mail
operation resolves through `resolveMailbox` (`lib/mail/imap.ts:244`): `requireUser()` at `:245`, only
mailboxes where `subscription.userId === user.id` (`:247`), and an explicitly requested address must
match one of them or it throws (`:270`).

**`Mailbox.address` is now `@unique` globally** (`prisma/schema.prisma:674`), with the schema comment
naming the cross-tenant takeover it closes — see the Business email chapter.

**What works.**

| Feature | Where |
|---|---|
| Folder list with roles and counts | `lib/actions-mail.ts:102`; `folderRole` `lib/mail/imap.ts:360` (SPECIAL-USE first, then name heuristics) |
| Message list, 50/page, IMAP SEARCH over subject/from/to/body | `lib/actions-mail.ts:153`, `:167` |
| Read, HTML sanitised, `\Seen` best-effort | `:229`, `safeHtml` `lib/mail/render.ts:25` |
| Flags, move, delete (→ Trash, then expunge) | `:521`, `:567` |
| Compose with attachments, ≤10 files / 20 MB | `:411`; caps `:318`; decode+validate `:355` |
| Attachment download by `<uid>:<part>` | `app/api/mail/attachment/route.ts:14` |
| Identity on outgoing mail — display name → `From`, `replyTo` → `Reply-To`, `organization` → header | `lib/actions-mail.ts:468-487` |
| Sent copy is byte-identical to what was sent (compiled once via `streamTransport`) | `:473-488` |
| Rich signature with image upload and size presets | `components/customer/mail/MailSettings.tsx:297`, `:655`, `:688` |
| Auto-reply and forwarding as **real Mailcow sieve** | `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:298`, `:388`, `:448`; compiler `lib/mail/sieve.ts` |
| Aliases (real Mailcow) | `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:522` |
| Mailbox password reveal + reset | `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:744`, `:776` |
| Orphan-mailbox adoption from Mailcow | `lib/mail/imap.ts:126` `discoverMailboxes` |
| CalDAV calendar + tasks | `lib/calendar/caldav.ts:51`, actions `lib/actions-calendar.ts:159` |

Sieve is worth a note: `lib/mail/sieve.ts` compiles **one managed script** (rationale at `:22`) with
markers (`:55`) so `getMailRuleStatus` (`lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:361`) derives status from the
**live script**, not from the DB. Rules are pushed to Mailcow *before* the DB write (`:416`), so the DB
can never claim a rule that the mail server does not have. `assertRulesAllowed` (`:336`) refuses
unverified external domains.

**What is missing.** No folder create/rename/delete anywhere. No draft saving — the only IMAP `append`
is the Sent copy (`lib/actions-mail.ts:504`).

**Honest note — the signature is appended in the browser.** `sendMessage` never touches it;
`components/customer/mail/Composer.tsx:165-186` does, fed by
`components/customer/mail/MailClient.tsx:124`. And `app/dashboard/mail/page.tsx:34` passes only the
legacy plain-text `signature` as `initialSignature`. So a signature set in the rich editor may not
appear on mail composed through a path that does not run that client-side append.

## Business email hosting and DKIM

**What it does.** Sells mailbox hosting on the platform's Mailcow appliance for a customer's own
domain: plan, DNS records, verification, mailboxes, quotas.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Business email · example.com                       Plan: Business (5 / 25GB)│
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ① VERIFY YOUR DOMAIN                                    ● Verified          │
│  ② DNS RECORDS                          [ Connect Cloudflare — do it for me ]│
│  ┌───────┬──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ TXT   │ _nxeon-verify.example.com│ nxeon-verify=a1b2c3…            ✓    │ │
│  │ MX 10 │ example.com              │ mail.nxeon.cloud                ✓    │ │
│  │ TXT   │ example.com              │ v=spf1 include:nxeon.cloud ~all ✓    │ │
│  │ TXT   │ dkim._domainkey.example… │ v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjAN…     ✓    │ │
│  │ TXT   │ _dmarc.example.com       │ v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:…  ✗    │ │
│  └───────┴──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│  ③ MAILBOXES                                              3 of 5 used        │
│  alice@example.com    10 GB   ACTIVE   [reveal pw] [reset pw] [settings]      │
│  billing@example.com  5 GB    ACTIVE   [reveal pw] [reset pw] [settings]      │
│  [ + Add mailbox ]                            [ Open inbox → ]               │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Mailcow client.** `/opt/nxeon/lib/mailcow.ts` — configuration read from env at call time
(`mailcowConfigured()` `:28`), `X-API-Key` auth, and critically `assertNoApiError` (`:100`) which
catches Mailcow's habit of returning **HTTP 200 with `type: "danger"`** in the body. Domain create
`:118`, mailbox create `:148`, set active `:167`, set password `:179`, delete `:195`, list `:222`,
aliases `:271`, sieve filters `:360`, stats `:490`. `MAILCOW_API_URL` and `MAILCOW_API_KEY` are set in
`.env`, so it is live.

**Provisioning.** `provisionMailboxOnMailcow` (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:87`): returns
`PROVISIONING` when Mailcow is unconfigured (`:93`), ensures the domain exists (`:101`), generates an
18-byte base64url password (`:107`), creates the mailbox (`:108`), then sets the row `ACTIVE` with
`passwordEnc` (`:116`) or `FAILED` (`:122`). It never throws. Called from `addMailbox` (`:572`), which
enforces the plan's mailbox cap (`:601`), sets the per-mailbox quota (`:611`), and **refuses external
domains that are not verified** (`:588`).

**The cross-tenant takeover this closed.** The pre-launch QA sweep found that any customer could take
over another customer's email domain, reset the password on their live mailboxes, and read and send as
them, for the price of the cheapest email plan. The chain was: the "one subscription per domain" check
was scoped to the **caller**, `EmailSubscription.domainName` had no unique constraint,
`Mailbox.address` had none either, and Mailcow keys mailboxes by **address** — so
`resetMailboxPassword` validated ownership of *the attacker's own row* and then set the password on the
victim's real mailbox. Now: the duplicate check is **global** (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:269-279`,
with the incident documented at `:259-268`) and `Mailbox.address` is `@unique`
(`prisma/schema.prisma:674`).

**DKIM is generated by Mailcow; this codebase only reads it.** `mcGetDkim` (`lib/mailcow.ts:426`) and
`mcGetDkimDetails` (`:443`) call `GET /get/dkim/<domain>` for `dkim_txt`, `dkim_selector`, `length`.
**There is no `/add/dkim` call anywhere in the repo.** Key generation is a side effect of
`mcCreateDomain` (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:370-372`). If Mailcow has no key, the DNS panel shows
an empty value plus an explanatory note (`:411`). Selector is the constant `DKIM_SELECTOR = "dkim"`
(`:44`). `EmailSubscription.dkimRecord` caches the value once (`:374`), but the deliverability path
deliberately reads the **live** key instead (`:537`, rationale `lib/mailcow.ts:433`).

**The five records** — `getEmailDnsRecords` (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:348`):

| Row | Host | Value | Line |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ownership | `_nxeon-verify.<domain>` TXT | `nxeon-verify=<verifyToken>` | `:385` |
| MX (prio 10) | apex | `mail.nxeon.cloud` | `:392` |
| SPF | apex TXT | `v=spf1 include:nxeon.cloud ~all` | `:399` |
| DKIM | `dkim._domainkey.<domain>` TXT | live/cached `dkim_txt` | `:406` |
| DMARC | `_dmarc.<domain>` TXT | `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@nxeon.cloud` | `:415` |

**Auto-creation** happens only through the customer's own Cloudflare, and only for **external**
domains: `autoCreateEmailDns` (`:868`) reuses `getEmailDnsRecords` as the single source (`:890`), finds
the zone (`:908`) and upserts (`:923`). Verification (`verifyEmailDomain` `:440`) treats the TXT token
as the primary signal (`:463`), with MX only corroborating.

**Plans.** `prisma/seed-email-plans.ts:26-30` — Starter 1 mailbox / 10 GB / $1.99, Business 5 / 25 /
$7.99, Pro 25 / 50 / $24.99, all `termMonths: 1`. Admin CRUD
`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:143-224`, all `requireArea("billing")`; delete refused while
subscriptions exist (`:213`). Renewals run in `worker/product-renewals.ts` — wallet only, no dunning,
and an unpaid subscription is `SUSPENDED` with **mailboxes kept** (`:210`), never deleted.

**Honest notes.**

- **In-account domains get no mail DNS published.** `components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:260-263`
  tells the customer that a domain registered with Nxeon has *"its mail DNS managed for you — mailboxes
  go live automatically."* Nothing publishes MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC at name.com:
  `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:283` only ever adds A records. Same defect class as the markup bug, and
  it affects whether their mail works at all.
- **`email_mx_host` and `email_spf_include` are saved and read by nothing.** The admin panel hint at
  `components/admin/settings/GeneralPanel.tsx:26` says *"Shown in the customer business-email DNS
  setup panel"* and `:34` says *"Rendered as `v=spf1 include:<value> ~all`"*. Both are false. The real
  values are hardcoded at `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:36` (`mail.nxeon.cloud`) and `:41`
  (`nxeon.cloud`), while the admin fields default to `mx.nxeon.email` and `_spf.nxeon.email`. An admin
  reading that panel would conclude mail is misconfigured, and editing either field changes nothing.
- **`app/admin/email-plans/page.tsx:38` still says "integration pending"** — stale; Mailcow is wired.
- Auto-reply/forwarding are real now, but **there is no per-mailbox "Log in" action** on the mailbox
  row — only a generic `/dashboard/mail` link, with no SSO handoff.

## Deliverability checking — and why you must not trust this box's resolver

**The trap, and it is specific to this host.** `/etc/nsswitch.conf:12` reads
`hosts: files myhostname dns`, and `/etc/hosts:7` contains:

```
51.79.162.96 ns5002569.ip-51-79-162.net ns5002569
```

So the **system resolver answers name and reverse lookups for this box out of a local file**. Any
deliverability check that goes through `getaddrinfo` will cheerfully report a PTR of
`ns5002569.ip-51-79-162.net` — the OVH default, which is precisely the broken forward-confirmed rDNS
that is blocking mail — or, worse, report whatever `/etc/hosts` says rather than what the world sees.
`/etc/resolv.conf:2` is `nameserver 213.186.33.99`, OVH's recursive resolver, which adds caching on
top.

**A deliverability check MUST query the zone's authoritative nameservers directly.**

**The good news: `lib/mail/deliverability.ts` does exactly that.** The trap is documented in its header
(`:12-28`) and implemented:

```
 lib/mail/deliverability.ts
 :30  import { Resolver } from "node:dns/promises";
 :33  BOOTSTRAP_RESOLVERS = ["1.1.1.1", "8.8.8.8", "9.9.9.9"]

 :65  bootstrapResolver()
 :69    // Explicit setServers is the entire point — a bare `new Resolver()`
 :70    // inherits /etc/resolv.conf, which is the failure mode above.
        r.setServers(BOOTSTRAP_RESOLVERS)

 :88  authoritativeResolver(domain)
 :94    for zone of [domain, ...parentZones(domain)]     ← handles sub-zones
 :96      ns  = boot.resolveNs(zone)                     ← NS via pinned public resolvers
 :111     ips = boot.resolve4(ns) / resolve6(ns)         ← NS names → IPs
 :122     resolver.setServers(ips)                       ← PINNED to the zone's OWN authority

 :206  every record then read off THAT resolver:
         resolver.resolveMx(domain)
         txtAt(resolver, domain)                  ← SPF
         txtAt(resolver, "dkim._domainkey."+domain)
         txtAt(resolver, "_dmarc."+domain)
 :131  txtAt treats NXDOMAIN/ENODATA as "not published", never as an error
 :348  the nameservers actually used are RETURNED, for auditability
```

Checks produced: MX (`:216`), SPF (`:248` — multiple SPF records is a hard fail at `:255`, accepts
`include:` or a bare `mx` at `:260`, and the `~all`/`-all` terminator gates pass vs warn at `:266`),
DKIM (`:288`, compares only the `p=` value via `dkimKey` `:141`), DMARC (`:319`).

**The precise mechanic, because it matters when you write the next check.** `/etc/hosts` and
`nsswitch` are consulted by `getaddrinfo`, i.e. Node's `dns.lookup()`. Node's `Resolver` /
`resolveTxt` / `resolveMx` / `reverse` (c-ares) **skip nsswitch** and use `/etc/resolv.conf` servers
instead. So there are two distinct wrong answers available on this box, and both are still reachable:

| Call site | What it uses | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:5` imports top-level `resolveTxt`, `resolveMx`; used at `:464`, `:474` | default resolver (213.186.33.99) | **Domain-ownership verification** can tell a customer who has just published `_nxeon-verify` that it is not there, purely from recursive-cache staleness |

## Teams and organizations

**What it does — stated precisely, because this used to be overstated.** An `Organization` has one
owner plus a set of `Membership` rows. A membership grants **visibility of the org roster**, and for
`OWNER`/`ADMIN` the right to invite, re-role and remove members. **It grants nothing else.**

The docblock at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-teams.ts:17-27` is unusually blunt and worth quoting:

> Servers, domains, volumes, game servers, billing and invoices all remain scoped to the account that
> owns them; no loader or action anywhere joins `Membership` to a resource. The per-member "dashboard
> areas" control that used to sit on this page **has been removed rather than left in place**:
> `Membership.areas` was written, echoed back as saved, and read by nothing, so an owner who
> restricted a member to Invoices was shown a restriction that did not exist.

That removal is the right pattern for this codebase: when a control cannot be enforced, delete the
control rather than leave a false affordance.

**Consent is enforced.** `inviteMember` emails an invitation; only `acceptInvite`, run by the invitee,
creates a `Membership` (`:29-31`). Nothing can add a person to an org they did not agree to join.
Tokens are signed with a TTL (`signInviteToken` / `verifyInviteToken` / `INVITE_TTL_HOURS`, all in
`/opt/nxeon/lib/team-guard.ts`). Every mutation verifies the actor holds a membership of the required
role in the target org (`canAdministerOrg`), so a hand-crafted request cannot touch someone else's org.

**Data model.** `Organization` (`prisma/schema.prisma:871`), `Membership` (`:880`).

**Honest note.** Shared billing and cross-account resource access **do not exist**. The
`emails.teamInvite` template has an `acceptUrl`, and that flow now genuinely exists — but a member
still sees none of the owner's servers. No dashboard page is org-scoped.

## Two-factor authentication — and why `lib/totp-verify.ts` is a plain module

**What it does.** RFC 6238 TOTP with hashed one-time backup codes, challenged at login, plus an
admin-settable requirement for staff.

```
 LOGIN
  ├─ 1. rate limit: login_ratelimit_max (default 10) per 15 min per email+IP
  │        lib/actions.ts:150
  ├─ 2. password check
  ├─ 3. if user.totpEnabled → 2FA challenge     lib/actions.ts:166
  │        verifyTotpForUser(userId, code)      lib/totp-verify.ts:50
  │          ├─ verifyTOTP(secret, code)                  → pass
  │          └─ else consume a matching backup code       → pass, code removed
  └─ 4. session cookie, session_length_days (default 30)   lib/auth.ts
```

**This is the most instructive security story in the codebase.** `verifyTotpForUser` used to live in
`lib/actions-2fa.ts`, which carries `"use server"` at the top. **Every export of such a module is a
registered, network-callable server action.** The docblock at `/opt/nxeon/lib/totp-verify.ts:6-23`
spells out what that meant:

> That made this function a public endpoint taking an arbitrary `userId`, performing no
> authentication, no ownership check and no rate limiting, returning a raw boolean — and mutating
> state, because a matching backup code is consumed. `login()` is throttled to 10 attempts per 15
> minutes per email+IP; calling this action directly bypassed that completely, allowing **unlimited
> TOTP and backup-code guessing against a named account**. Victim user IDs were obtainable from the
> team page.

So `lib/totp-verify.ts` is **deliberately a plain module**. It has no `"use server"`, which means there
is no action ID for a client to call — it can only be reached by server code that imports it. There
are exactly two importers: `lib/actions-2fa.ts:10` (the management actions) and `lib/actions.ts:28`
(the login flow). The file ends with an instruction: **"Do NOT re-export any of this from a
`"use server"` module."** Honour it.

The function itself carries the matching contract (`:44-48`): callers **must** have already established
that the request is entitled to attempt a 2FA check for this user, and **must** apply their own rate
limiting — *"this function deliberately has neither, which is precisely why it must never be exposed as
a server action."*

**Entry points.** `lib/totp.ts` (dependency-free RFC 6238), `lib/totp-verify.ts` (`hashCode` `:26`,
`totpSecretOf` `:33`, `verifyTotpForUser` `:50`), `lib/actions-2fa.ts` (enrol, disable, regenerate
codes), `lib/actions.ts:150` (throttle) and `:166` (challenge). Secrets are stored encrypted
(`totpSecretEnc`) with a legacy plaintext fallback so already-enrolled users keep working
(`totp-verify.ts:33`). Backup codes are sha256-hashed and consumption is audit-logged
(`user.2fa_backup_code_used`, `:63`). Staff enforcement: `enforce_staff_2fa`, read by
`app/admin/layout.tsx`. Tests: `/opt/nxeon/test/totp.test.ts`, `/opt/nxeon/test/rate-limit.test.ts`.

**The general lesson.** Anything exported from a `lib/actions-*.ts` file is a public POST endpoint. Ask
of every export: *if an anonymous caller invoked this with arbitrary arguments, what happens?* This
same file convention also caused the E352 Files-tab error by exporting a non-async value.

## Bandwidth and abuse detection

**What it does.** Meters each VM's network transfer from Proxmox counters, shows it against the plan
allowance, and raises an abuse alert on a sustained outbound spike.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Billing · Transfer this cycle                                         │
│  web-01     ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  312 GB / 8 TB   4%               │
│             period 2026-07-14 → now (metering began 2026-07-26)        │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

 worker/monitor.ts:447  monitorSweep()  every 10 min
   :456  sampleServerBandwidth()   ← runs FIRST, inside monitorSweep, on purpose
   …     node disk warnings, service checks, backup freshness
 worker/index.ts:1106  monitorSweep()
 worker/index.ts:~1090 abuseSweep()   ← reads counters from THIS sweep, not the last
```

**Metering.** `/opt/nxeon/lib/bandwidth.ts` is the one place that decides how Proxmox `netin`/`netout`
become `Server.bwInBytes` / `bwOutBytes`, and how much confidence a usage figure may project. Two hard
rules, both stated at `:14-32`:

1. **Never invent traffic.** Proxmox counters are cumulative per **QEMU process**, not per VM lifetime
   — a stop/start, reset, reinstall or live migration replaces the process and the counters restart at
   0. A naive `cur − prev` then goes hugely negative, or (when the fresh boot has already pushed more
   than the stale baseline held) hugely positive. `creditFromCounters` detects the restart and credits
   only bytes it can prove happened inside the interval.
2. **Never present a partial period as authoritative.** The meter only knows traffic from the moment it
   started sampling. `bwUsageView` reports the period it actually covers and **refuses to render a
   percentage at all** when no sample has ever been taken — because *"a `0 B / 20 TB · 0%` that means
   'we never looked' is exactly the defect class this codebase keeps repeating."*

The sweep is at `/opt/nxeon/worker/monitor.ts:205` (`sampleServerBandwidth`), with gap detection and
bounded backfill (`:340-352`), a period roll at `BW_PERIOD_MS` (`:377`), and a **window fix** at `:361`
that pulls `bwWindowStart` forward to the moment measurement actually began — *"without this the UI
would claim these bytes cover months we never watched."*

**Abuse detection.** `/opt/nxeon/worker/abuse.ts` compares `bwOutBytes` against `abuseBwMark` /
`abuseBwMarkAt` to compute a sustained Mbps, re-marks every sweep regardless of outcome, skips counter
resets (negative delta) and windows under 30 s, and raises one **open** `AbuseAlert` per
server+`BANDWIDTH_SPIKE` so admins are not spammed. `severity: HIGH` at ≥3× the threshold. Settings:
`abuse_outbound_mbps` (default 200) and `abuse_autosuspend` (default false), both genuinely read.
Admin queue `/admin/abuse`; manual suspension `lib/actions-abuse.ts:27` (`suspendForAbuse`, sets
`suspendReason: "ABUSE"`).

**Data model.** `Server.bwInBytes`, `bwOutBytes`, `bwWindowStart`, `abuseBwMark`, `abuseBwMarkAt`
(`prisma/schema.prisma:347-353`); `AbuseAlert` (`:1022`); `ServerDiskSample` (`:1145`) for the
disk-usage-over-time chart.

**Honest notes.**

- **This landed today and is mid-integration.** Both columns shipped with `@default(0)` and **nothing
  ever wrote them**. The consequences, recorded in `lib/bandwidth.ts:6-13`: the billing panel titled
  *"Transfer used this cycle … versus plan allowance"* read a permanent `0 B / 20 TB · 0%`, and
  `worker/abuse.ts` computed its rate from `bwOutBytes` deltas, so `deltaBytes` was always 0 and
  **`BANDWIDTH_SPIKE` could never fire** — the platform shipped an abuse detector that could not
  detect anything, with two admin-settable knobs on a dead sensor. The metering sweep now exists and
  is wired.
- **The billing page has not adop`bwUsageView` yet.** `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:56` still does
  `Number(s.bwInBytes) + Number(s.bwOutBytes)` directly, so rule 2 above — never present a partial
  period as authoritative — is not yet honoured on the surface it was written for. `bwUsageView` has no
  consumer.
- **The automatic abuse suspension does not set `suspendReason`.** `worker/abuse.ts` enqueues a bare
  `SUSPEND` job; only the manual admin path sets `"ABUSE"`. See the suspension-reasons chapter.

| Platform | `/admin/settings`, `/admin/staff`, `/admin/audit`, `/admin/logs`, `/admin/automation`, `/admin/improvements`, `/admin/email-templates`, `/admin/mail`, `/admin/domains`, `/admin/games`, `/admin/blog`, `/admin/newsletter`, `/admin/testimonials`, `/admin/docs` |

**The four you will use most when something is wrong:**

| Page | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| `/admin/jobs` | Every `Job` with `type`, `status`, `attempts`, `step`, `error`. First stop for anything that "did nothing". |
| `/admin/servers/[id]` | The full row: status, `suspendReason`, `dunningStage`, `expiresAt`, `extraDiskGB`, volumes, jobs. |
| `/admin/logs` | The `EmailLog` — what was actually sent, to whom, and whether it errored. |
| `/admin/audit` | `AuditLog` — every privileged action, including impersonated ones attributed to the real admin. |

**Impersonation.** `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target and
`realUser()` the actual admin. A banner and exit control are handled in

impersonating**. Every money-spending action is blocked while impersonating —
`lib/actions.ts:235`, `:382`, `:491`, `:591`, `lib/actions-disk.ts:41`,
`lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts:133`, `lib/actions-2fa.ts:78`.

unsettable.

## RBAC — roles, areas and impersonation

**What it does.** The admin portal is divided into seven **areas**; each area maps to the staff roles
allowed to use it. `ADMIN` implicitly has every area.

```
 Role      overview  analytics  clients  support  fleet  billing  platform
 ───────   ────────  ─────────  ───────  ───────  ─────  ───────  ────────
 CUSTOMER      ·         ·         ·        ·       ·       ·         ·
 SUPPORT       ✓         ·         ✓        ✓       ·       ·         ·
 BILLING       ✓         ·         ·        ·       ·       ✓         ·
 ADMIN         ✓         ✓         ✓        ✓       ✓       ✓         ✓
```

`AREA_ROLES` at `/opt/nxeon/lib/rbac.ts:26`; `canAccess` at `:34`; `isStaff` at `:39`.

(`:85`). A new admin page is therefore locked down by default, which is the right failure direction.

`requireArea` redirects: signed out → `/login`; a non-staff user → `/dashboard`; a staff user without
the area → `/admin`. It returns the **real** signed-in user, not the impersonation target.

# Part III — Admin runbooks

Copy-pasteable procedures. Every one of these has a wrong way that has already caused an incident on
this box, so the warnings are not decorative.

## Runbook — deploying a change

**Never build in the production tree while a background agent is also building it.** That race
corrupts `.next` output and has already caused a live styling outage.

```bash
# 1. Commit. The post-commit hook auto-pushes to GitHub.
cd /opt/nxeon
git status                      # confirm you know every changed file
git add -A && git commit -m "…"

# 2. Staging first.
/opt/nxeon/scripts/deploy-staging.sh            # or: deploy-staging.sh <ref>
#    builds + prisma db push + restarts nxeon-staging-web / -worker
curl -sI http://51.79.162.96:8080/ | head -1    # verify staging answers
journalctl -u nxeon-staging-worker -n 50 --no-pager

# 3. Promote.
/opt/nxeon/scripts/promote-production.sh        # rebuild + restart production

# 4. Verify.
systemctl is-active nxeon-web nxeon-worker
curl -sI https://nxeon.cloud/ | head -1
curl -s  https://nxeon.cloud/api/health
journalctl -u nxeon-worker -n 50 --no-pager
```

**Rules.**

- `npm run build` **must pass** before restarting anything. There is no CI and nothing enforces this.
- After a `prisma/schema.prisma` change: `npm run db:push`. Staging has its own database
  (`nxeon_staging`) — push there first.
- `git status` before every deploy. Several agents write into this tree concurrently; `HEAD` does not
  always describe what is on disk, and whoever deploys next ships whatever is sitting there.
- Never restart the worker without doing the queue check in the next runbook.

## Runbook — restarting services safely

**NEVER restart the worker while a job is RUNNING.** A migration takes ~24 minutes; killing it
mid-flight destroyed a customer's first attempt. `reapStuckJobs()`
(`/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:1008`) will requeue the job if `attempts < 3` — but for a migration that
is useless, because the source SSH password was already scrubbed, so the retry fails at
`worker/migrate-real.ts:3318`.

**Always run the queue check first:**

```bash
# Is anything in flight?
sudo -u postgres psql -d nxeon -c "
  SELECT id, type, status, attempts, progress, step,
         age(now(), \"updatedAt\") AS stalled_for
  FROM \"Job\"
  WHERE status IN ('RUNNING','QUEUED')
  ORDER BY \"createdAt\";"
```

```
 result empty                     → safe to restart
 rows with status = QUEUED only   → safe (they have not started)
 ANY row with status = RUNNING    → DO NOT RESTART
        │
        ├─ type = MIGRATE   → wait it out. Up to ~40 min. Watch:
        │                      journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f
        ├─ type = BACKUP_*  → wait. Check progress in the same query.
        ├─ type = DISK_EXPAND / RESIZE → wait; these touch a live disk.
        └─ stalled_for > 45 min and no log output for 10 min → genuinely wedged,
                                see the stuck-job runbook before restarting.
```

```bash
# Only after the check comes back clear:
systemctl restart nxeon-worker
journalctl -u nxeon-worker -n 30 --no-pager      # expect: "provisioning worker starting"
                                                 #         "port forwards synced"
```

**Restarting the web tier is safe at any time** — it holds no job state:

```bash
systemctl restart nxeon-web
```

**Other units.** `nxeon-terminal` and `nxeon-console-proxy` drop live sessions when restarted but
nothing else. `nxeon-firewall` re-applies `scripts/firewall.nft`; prefer
`scripts/firewall-safe-apply.sh`, which has a rollback timer, over applying rules by hand.

**Never edit the `NXEON_FWD` iptables chain manually** — `worker/network.ts` rebuilds it from the
database, so your change disappears at the next `syncPortForwards()`.

## Runbook — reading worker logs

```bash
journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f                      # follow
journalctl -u nxeon-worker --since "1 hour ago"    # window
journalctl -u nxeon-worker -n 500 --no-pager | less
journalctl -u nxeon-staging-worker -f              # staging
```

**The prefixes, and what each means:**

| Prefix | Source | Read it when |
|---|---|---|
| `[worker]` | `worker/index.ts` — loop, claims, reaping, IP pool | anything queue-shaped |
| `[billing]` | `worker/billing.ts` | renewals, dunning, suspensions |
| `[product-billing]` | `worker/product-renewals.ts` | email/volume renewals |
| `[backup]` | `worker/index.ts:762` | prune counts |
| `[backup-schedule]` | `worker/backup-schedule.ts` | scheduled backups enqueued |
| `[monitor]` | `worker/monitor.ts` | node disk, service checks, disk samples |
| `[bandwidth]` | `worker/monitor.ts` / `lib/bandwidth.ts` | transfer metering |
| `[abuse]` | `worker/abuse.ts` | outbound spikes |
| `[geo]` | `worker/geo.ts` | visit enrichment |
| `[game-update]` | `worker/game-update.ts` | 6-hourly game sweeps |
| `[game-config]` | `worker/game-config.ts` | settings apply |

**Grep patterns that pay off:**

```bash
# A sweep has quietly stopped happening — every sweep is individually try/caught,
# so a permanently broken one is invisible outside the journal.
journalctl -u nxeon-worker --since today | grep -i "sweep error"

# One server's whole story
journalctl -u nxeon-worker --since "2 days ago" | grep <hostname>

# Jobs that were reaped after a restart
journalctl -u nxeon-worker | grep "reaped stuck job"

# Migration progress lines (they carry the percentage and the step)
journalctl -u nxeon-worker --since "1 hour ago" | grep -i migrat
```

**Backup and restore health is NOT in the journal** — it is in files nothing reads:

```bash
cat /tank/backup/status/verify-restore.json
cat /tank/backup/status/vm-backup.json
cat /tank/backup/status/host-config.json
cat /tank/backup/status/offsite.json
journalctl -u nxeon-backup-vms -u nxeon-verify-restore --since "2 days ago"
```

## Runbook — diagnosing a stuck job

**Symptom:** a customer says a button does nothing, or a server sits in `PROVISIONING` /
`REINSTALLING` / `DELETING`, or an SSL certificate sits `PENDING`.

```
 1. IS THE WORKER ALIVE?
    systemctl is-active nxeon-worker
    journalctl -u nxeon-worker -n 20 --no-pager
        │
        ├─ dead ──────────► start it. reapStuckJobs() runs on boot and will
        │                   requeue anything under 3 attempts.
        └─ alive ─────────► 2

 2. WHAT IS IT DOING RIGHT NOW?
    the queue-check SQL from the restart runbook
        │
        ├─ a long RUNNING job (MIGRATE, BACKUP_*) ─► NOT STUCK. It is serial.
        │      Everything else queues behind it. Tell the customer the ETA.
        │      This is the #1 cause of "SSL stuck pending" — a cert once sat
        │      PENDING for 13m15s behind a 24-minute migration.
        └─ nothing RUNNING but rows QUEUED ────────► 3

 3. IS THE SERVER BLOCKED BY ITS OWN GUARD?
    One in-flight job per server. A row left RUNNING blocks every later action
    on that server forever.
        SELECT * FROM "Job" WHERE "serverId" = '<id>' ORDER BY "createdAt" DESC;
        │
        └─ a RUNNING row with updatedAt hours old and no log output
                 → genuinely orphaned. Restart the worker: reapStuckJobs
                   requeues it (attempts < 3) or FAILS it and reconciles the
                   money. This is why a worker restart "fixes" wedged servers.

 4. IT FAILED — WHAT WAS THE REASON?
    SELECT type, status, attempts, step, error FROM "Job" WHERE id = '<id>';
    /admin/jobs shows the same fields.
        │
        ├─ type ∈ VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS  → the server is ERROR, correctly
        └─ money involved → confirm the reconcile ran:
             SELECT * FROM "AuditLog"
              WHERE action LIKE '%reconcile%' AND detail LIKE '%<serverId>%';
             SELECT * FROM "WalletTransaction"
              WHERE description LIKE 'Refund%' ORDER BY "createdAt" DESC;
```

**Never hand-edit a `Job` row to `DONE`.** The handler's side effects (VM state, wallet, invoice,
notification) did not happen; you would only be hiding it.

## Runbook — re-running a failed migration

**There is no re-run.** Read that before you go looking for a button.

```
 A failed migration CANNOT be re-enqueued:
   worker/migrate.ts:555  clearSecrets() ran on failure
   → the source SSH password is gone
   → migrate-real.ts:3318 throws "source SSH password is missing or could not
     be decrypted" on any retry of the same migrationId
   Also: no admin page, no retry action, and the handler swallows the error
   (migrate.ts:562) so MAX_ATTEMPTS never engages.
```

**The supported procedure:**

```
 1. READ WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED. The itemised results are in the DB, not the UI.
      SELECT status, progress, step, "lastError" FROM "Migration"
       WHERE id = '<id>';
      SELECT jsonb_pretty(items::jsonb) FROM "Migration" WHERE id = '<id>';
    → items.results is an array of { step, status, detail }, with the outcome
      line as the FIRST entry. Statuses: running | copied | failed | skipped.

 2. THE DUMPS ARE STILL ON THE TARGET. migrate-real.ts:5324 keeps them on
    purpose so a failed import can be retried by hand:
      ssh -p <sshPort> root@51.79.162.96
      ls -la /root/nxeon-migrations/<migrationId>/dumps/
      mysql --force < mysql-all.sql          # or
      sudo -u postgres psql -f pg-all.sql
    Reference copies of the source's web config:
      /root/nxeon-migrations/<id>/source-nginx/
      /root/nxeon-migrations/<id>/nginx-before/     ← pre-change snapshot
      /root/nxeon-migrations/<id>/apache-before/

 3. FIX THE NAMED BLOCKER. Every blocker carries a copy-paste command:
      unit won't start → the missing ExecStart binary, and the symlink to make
      masked web server → the exact `systemctl unmask` line
      missing cert     → the certbot command at the referenced path

 4. RETRY TLS WITHOUT RE-COPYING ANYTHING (the one supported re-enqueue):
      INSERT INTO "Job" (id, type, status, payload, "createdAt", "updatedAt")
      VALUES (gen_random_uuid()::text, 'MIGRATE', 'QUEUED',
              '{"migrationId":"<id>","phase":"tls"}'::jsonb, now(), now());
    Idempotent via certbot --keep-until-expiring; copies nothing; deliberately
    does NOT touch Migration.status.  (worker/migrate.ts:245-258)
    ⚠ This is the ONLY thing that re-runs a TLS pass — runPostCutoverTls has no
      other caller anywhere. Pointing DNS does not trigger it.

 5. IF THE STACK ITSELF NEEDS REDOING: start a NEW migration from the wizard
    ("← Start another migration", MigrationWizard.tsx:1436) with freshly entered
    credentials. Re-runs are idempotent by construction — user/group creation,
    volume create, image present-checks and the Docker pre-flight allowance all
    handle a second pass. Rate limit: 5 per 10 minutes.

 6. ROLLBACK = point the A record back at the old server. There is deliberately
    no undo on the new one, so the cutover can be retried the moment the problem
    is fixed. The DNS card renders for every terminal state, FAILED included.
```

## Runbook — issuing a certificate by hand

Use this when `SSL_ISSUE` keeps failing, or after a migration to pick up names whose DNS moved after
the run finished (which nothing retries automatically).

```bash
# 0. Preconditions — check these first, they are 90% of failures.
dig +short A example.com @1.1.1.1        # must be 51.79.162.96 (or the VM's IP)
                                         # ⚠ do NOT use `dig example.com` with no
                                         # @server on this box — see the mail
                                         # deliverability runbook for why.
# Cloudflare proxy must be OFF (grey cloud): HTTP-01 cannot validate through it.

# 1. Get onto the VM.
sudo -u postgres psql -d nxeon -t -c \
  "SELECT hostname, \"ipAddress\", \"sshPort\" FROM \"Server\" WHERE hostname='<host>';"
ssh -p <sshPort> root@51.79.162.96

# 2. Port 80 must be free — certbot --standalone binds it itself.
ss -ltnp | grep ':80 '
systemctl stop nginx        # if nginx holds it

# 3. Issue. This is the exact command the worker runs (worker/ssl.ts:420).
certbot certonly --standalone -n --agree-tos \
  -m nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com -d example.com

# 4. PROVE it exists and read the REAL expiry (never compute one).
openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem

# 5. --standalone does NOT install into nginx. Wire it up:
#    ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem;
#    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem;
nginx -t && systemctl start nginx

# 6. Verify what the server ACTUALLY presents for that name (SNI matters).
openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:443 -servername example.com </dev/null 2>/dev/null \
  | openssl x509 -noout -subject -ext subjectAltName -enddate
```

**Then reconcile the database**, because nothing sweeps it:

```sql
UPDATE "SslCertificate"
   SET status = 'ACTIVE',
       "issuedAt"  = now(),
       "expiresAt" = '<the notAfter you just READ, not one you calculated>',
       "lastError" = NULL
 WHERE domain = 'example.com';
```

**A wildcard (`*.example.com`) cannot be issued this way.** HTTP-01 cannot validate a wildcard. Use
DNS-01 with the customer's Cloudflare token — that ladder exists only inside the migration engine
(`worker/migrate-real.ts:2991` `issueDns01`).

**Remember: nothing renews.** `sslRenewalSweep` is written and never called, so every certificate
issued today — by the worker or by hand — will lapse at 90 days with no warning. Until that sweep is
wired, either keep the box's own `certbot.timer` doing the renewal in-guest, or diarise it.

## Runbook — checking mail deliverability

**⚠ READ THIS FIRST. This box's system resolver will lie to you.**

```
 /etc/nsswitch.conf:12   hosts:  files myhostname dns
 /etc/hosts:7            51.79.162.96 ns5002569.ip-51-79-162.net ns5002569
 /etc/resolv.conf:2      nameserver 213.186.33.99      (OVH recursive, cached)
```

Consequences you must design around:

- `getaddrinfo` (i.e. `ping`, `host` in some builds, Node's `dns.lookup()`) answers **name and reverse
  lookups for this host out of `/etc/hosts`**.
- c-ares (`dig` with no `@server`, Node's `Resolver`/`resolveTxt`/`resolveMx`/`reverse`) skips
  `nsswitch` but uses `/etc/resolv.conf`, so you get **OVH's cache**, not the zone.

**So every deliverability check MUST be aimed at the zone's authoritative nameservers.** That is
exactly what `lib/mail/deliverability.ts` does (`:65` pins `1.1.1.1`/`8.8.8.8`/`9.9.9.9` as bootstrap,
`:88` resolves the zone's own NS records and then `:122 resolver.setServers(ips)`), and it is what you
must do by hand.

```bash
D=example.com

# 1. Find the zone's OWN nameservers, via a pinned public resolver.
NS=$(dig +short NS "$D" @1.1.1.1 | head -1)
echo "authority: $NS"

# 2. Ask THAT nameserver for everything. @$NS is not optional.
dig +short MX  "$D"                   @"$NS"
dig +short TXT "$D"                   @"$NS"   # SPF: v=spf1 include:nxeon.cloud ~all
dig +short TXT "dkim._domainkey.$D"   @"$NS"   # DKIM: v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=…
dig +short TXT "_dmarc.$D"            @"$NS"   # DMARC: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=…
dig +short TXT "_nxeon-verify.$D"     @"$NS"   # ownership token

# 3. PTR / forward-confirmed reverse DNS — the platform has NO check for this.
#    NEVER use `dig -x` bare, and never `host`/`ping`: /etc/hosts answers.
dig +short -x 51.79.162.96 @1.1.1.1                 # expect mail.nxeon.cloud.
dig +short A "$(dig +short -x 51.79.162.96 @1.1.1.1 | sed 's/\.$//')" @1.1.1.1
#    FCrDNS is only satisfied when that A record comes back 51.79.162.96.
```

**What "broken" looks like here.** The known failure is `PTR[51.79.162.96] = ns5002569…` — the OVH
default. That is a **forward-confirmed reverse DNS failure** and it is why mail is being rejected. It
can only be fixed in the OVH control panel (or via `scripts/set-mail-ptr.ts`, which sets it and does
**not** verify it). No amount of IP warm-up compensates for it, so do not warm the IP first.

```bash
# 4. What Mailcow actually did with a message.
sudo -u postgres psql -d nxeon -c \
  'SELECT "createdAt", "to", subject, template, error
     FROM "EmailLog" ORDER BY "createdAt" DESC LIMIT 20;'
#    Then on the Mailcow VM (8000): postfix + rspamd logs.

# 5. Send a real test through the platform's own sender.
npx tsx /opt/nxeon/scripts/diag-email.ts        # sends, then reads back EmailLog
#    ⚠ This does NO DNS work at all. It proves SMTP, not deliverability.
```

**Also true and worth knowing:** the platform's own correct checker,
`checkEmailDeliverability` (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:523`), has **no caller** — there is no UI
button. And **domain-ownership verification** (`:464`, `:474`) uses the default resolver rather than
authority, so a customer who has just published `_nxeon-verify` can be told it is not there. If a
verification is failing and step 2 above shows the token present, that is why: wait for OVH's cache, or
re-run the check later.

## Runbook — rolling back

**Code rollback.**

```bash
cd /opt/nxeon
git log --oneline -20
git status                      # ⚠ uncommitted agent changes? stash them, do not lose them
git stash push -u -m "pre-rollback working tree"

git checkout <good-sha>         # or: git revert <bad-sha> to keep history forward-only
npm run build                   # MUST pass
# queue check from the restart runbook, THEN:
systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker
systemctl is-active nxeon-web nxeon-worker
curl -s https://nxeon.cloud/api/health
```

**Schema rollback.** `prisma db push` is not migration-versioned. A rollback that removes a column is
destructive.

```
 removing a column  → data in it is GONE. Take a dump first:
     bash /opt/nxeon/scripts/backup-db.sh
 adding a column    → safe to leave in place; old code ignores it.
 PREFER: roll the code back and leave the schema forward-compatible.
```

**Database rollback.** `scripts/verify-restore.sh` proves the newest dump restores, so this path is
tested daily.

```bash
ls -la /tank/backup/db/                       # newest nxeon-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.sql.gz
systemctl stop nxeon-web nxeon-worker         # queue check first
sudo -u postgres psql -c 'ALTER DATABASE nxeon RENAME TO nxeon_before_rollback;'
sudo -u postgres createdb nxeon
gunzip -c /tank/backup/db/nxeon-<stamp>.sql.gz | sudo -u postgres psql -d nxeon
systemctl start nxeon-web nxeon-worker
```

**Never roll the DB back without thinking about Proxmox.** VMs, disks and volumes are *not* in the
database. Restoring an older dump can leave `Server` rows pointing at VMIDs that were since deleted, or
lose rows for VMs that still exist. Cross-check:

```bash
qm list
sudo -u postgres psql -d nxeon -c \
  'SELECT vmid, hostname, status FROM "Server" WHERE vmid IS NOT NULL ORDER BY vmid;'
```

**Whole-box rollback.** Platform archives are in `/tank/backup/platform` (daily, keep 3), including
`host-config-*.tar.gz` with `/etc/pve` and every VM definition. `qmrestore` a guest from there. Note
that the off-site job is **not configured**, so `/tank` is a single point of failure — a chassis loss
loses every backup.

**Domain / nginx rollback.** Never hand-edit `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/*`. Fix
`/etc/nxeon/domains.env` and re-run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`, which regenerates every vhost,
re-obtains certificates, rewrites `APP_URL` in both `.env` files and restarts web.

# Part IV — Troubleshooting

Symptom → cause → fix. Mined from `docs/AUDIT-24H.md`, `docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md` and
`docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md`, then re-verified against the current tree. Where a row describes
something still broken, it says so.

## Troubleshooting — billing, checkout and money

| Symptom | Cause | Fix / where to look |
|---|---|---|
| Card charged, no server, no error | The old confirm/webhook race: fulfilment was gated on who won the *wallet-credit* race. **Fixed** by `FulfilledSession` | `SELECT * FROM "FulfilledSession" WHERE "stripeSessionId"='cs_…'` — `FAILED` carries `detail`; `CLAIMED` and stuck means fulfilment threw before settling |
| Customer closed the tab before the redirect | Same class; the redirect is not the fulfilment trigger any more | The webhook fulfils independently (`app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:34`) |
| Displayed price ≠ charged price | Promo applied on one side only. Both sides apply it now, but by **duplication** — `promoPriceCents` is reimplemented client-side, and there is no server-side `expectedCents` binding | Compare `Invoice.lineItems` against `vpsTermPriceCents` × the promo live at `Invoice.createdAt`. A wizard left open across a promo boundary can still diverge |
| Upgrade cost more than buying the plan outright | Proration used the raw list delta while purchase applied term + promo discounts. **Fixed** — one shared function | `lib/proration.ts:45`; the $1,044.45-vs-$665.08 case is in the docblock at `:30` |
| Downgrade credited more than was ever paid | Same root cause, mirror direction. **Fixed**; downgrades are also blocked today | `lib/resize.ts:65`, `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:161` |
| "Insufficient balance" with money on screen | Balance changed between quote and order; `debitWallet` is a guarded `updateMany` and fails closed | `lib/wallet.ts:21` |
| Coupon promised a bonus on a card top-up, nothing arrived | The cookie was read only by the demo gateway, which refuses in production; the Checkout session carried no `discounts` | **Verify before promising.** `app/api/stripe/checkout/route.ts` |
| Invoice shows Tax $0.00 with a tax rate configured | `applyTaxFromSettings` has one call site — an admin MRR display. No invoice creator passes `taxCents` | `lib/tax.ts:91`, `app/admin/products/page.tsx:93`. Tax is **not charged** |
| Invoice number has no prefix | `invoice_prefix` is saved and read by nothing; the renderer hardcodes `#` + a 5-digit pad | `lib/invoices.ts:147` |
| Renewal suspended a customer with a good card | **The card path cannot fire — there is no UI to save a card.** Every renewal is wallet-only today | `lib/actions-payment-method.ts` has zero callers |
| Refund guessed the wrong payment | The refund control did not send the invoice id | **Fixed** — `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts:61` |
| Admin suspended a paid-up customer and 13 days later the VM was deleted | `terminateOverdue` matched on `status: SUSPENDED` alone while the renewal sweep excludes suspended servers | **Fixed** — both paths scope to `suspendReason: "UNPAID"`. `worker/billing.ts:1333`, `lib/actions.ts:690` |
| A suspended spammer paid and came straight back | `renewNow` auto-unsuspended any suspension | **Fixed** — same two lines |

## Troubleshooting — provisioning and the worker

| Symptom | Cause | Fix / where to look |
|---|---|---|
| Button does nothing, no error | One in-flight job per server; a `RUNNING` row blocks every later action | Queue-check SQL in the restart runbook; a worker restart trips `reapStuckJobs` |
| SSL "stuck pending" for many minutes | The worker is a **strictly serial** single-job queue; the cert is behind a long job. One cert sat `PENDING` 13m15s behind a 24-minute migration | Not a bug, a design limit. Queue position is resolved at `app/dashboard/ssl/page.tsx:44` |
| Server stuck `PROVISIONING`/`REINSTALLING`/`DELETING` | Worker died mid-job | `reapStuckJobs()` `worker/index.ts:1008` requeues under 3 attempts, else `ERROR` + reconcile |
| A backup shut the server down | `BACKUP_CREATE` was treated as a VM-state failure | **Fixed** — excluded from `VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS` (`worker/index.ts:49`); backups use `mode: "snapshot"` (`:737`) |
| A failed disk expansion marked the server `ERROR` | `DISK_EXPAND` was in the failure set | **Fixed** — deliberately absent (`worker/index.ts:44`); money unwound by `reconcileFailedDiskExpand` (`:822`) |
| Customer holds extra disk; a plan resize hard-fails | Resize computed the target as `plan.diskGB`, i.e. a *shrink* | **Fixed** — worker resizes to `plan.diskGB + extraDiskGB` (`worker/index.ts:559`) |
| Reinstall wiped an attached volume | No guard | **Fixed** — `worker/index.ts:428-448`, `lib/actions.ts:464-471` |
| `RUNNING` but no SSH | `status: RUNNING` is written right after Proxmox accepts `start` — it proves nothing about the guest | Web console first. Then `PortForward` vs `iptables -t nat -L NXEON_FWD -n`. A failed cloud-init snippet write does not fail the job (`worker/index.ts:274`) |
| New server has no IP / VMID | Pool exhausted, or a deleted row still holds the UNIQUE `ipAddress` | `lib/ipam.ts`; release logic `worker/index.ts:988` |
| Staging touched a production VM | Wrong `NXEON_IP_START/END` or `NXEON_NAT_CHAIN` in `/opt/nxeon-staging/.env` | Staging is `.50–.99` / `30000–30999` / `NXEON_FWD_STG` / tag `nxeon-staging`. Nothing else separates them |
| A scheduled thing stopped happening | Every sweep is individually `try`/`catch`ed, so a permanently broken one is silent | `journalctl -u nxeon-worker --since today \| grep -i "sweep error"` |

## Troubleshooting — migration

Numbers in brackets are the item numbers in `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md`.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix (implemented in the engine) |
|---|---|---|
| A generated vhost is silently ignored [1] | The source's `nginx.conf` overwrote the target's, so `include sites-enabled/*` disappeared | Write where the **live** `nginx.conf` actually includes, then prove it with `nginx -T \| grep -F` — `nginx -t` passing is not proof (`migrate-real.ts:4638`) |
| `bind() to <old-ip>:80 failed (99)` [2] | Hardcoded source IP in ~21 configs | Rewrite source IP → target IP, or generate without IP binding (`:2769` stale sweep) |
| Web server down after migration [3] | Vhosts referenced certs that were never migrated | `/etc/letsencrypt` is migrated (`:3985`), or TLS blocks stripped and re-issued. Never leave a config referencing a missing cert |
| `http2 on;` unknown directive [4] | nginx ≥1.25 syntax on 1.18 | `nginx -v` parsed; directive folded into `listen` (`:4610`) |
| 502 on all traffic [6] | A copied catch-all `default` server with a dead upstream hijacked everything | Detected and disabled (`:4449`) |
| `ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID` [7] | An IP-bound `listen <ip>:80` block beats a generic `listen 80` regardless of `server_name` | Generated vhosts bind the target IP on **both** 80 and 443 when copied configs do (`:4615`) |
| `invalid PID number ""` [8] | Stale nginx PID after a config swap | `restart`, never `reload`, then check `is-active` (`:4663`) |
| Tenant subdomains get the wrong cert [9] | Multi-tenant wildcard not covered | `server_name *.<base>` added from copied env (`:4572`); **a wildcard needs DNS-01** — HTTP-01 cannot issue it |
| A container can never start [10] | Locally-built image, never in a registry | `docker save \| gzip` → `docker load` (`:1437`); prefer `docker pull` for public images |
| Page loads, nothing works [11] | Frameworks bake the API URL into the static bundle at build time | Old-hostname references detected in copied env (`:4353`); offer to rewrite **and rebuild** |
| Compose starts with empty secrets [12] | Real env file was `prod.env`, used via `--env-file` | `composeEnvFor` (`:4128`) resolves the real file and **refuses to start** when placeholders would resolve empty (`:4179`) |
| Unit crash-looped 880× / 78× with `203/EXEC` [13, 25] | `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/node`; the target has `/usr/bin/node` | `preflightUnitExecs` (`:2455`) before **every** enable: symlink, else copy from source, else **do not enable** and record a blocker |
| `Could not find a production build` [14, 26] | `.next` copied with no valid build | `unitHealthGate` (`:2570`) samples `NRestarts` twice; the Next.js message is recognised and answered with `next build` |
| Access denied despite the data being there [15] | The dump skips the `mysql` schema, so app DB users vanish | Grants replayed from password hashes on the target, then **confirmed by querying the target** (`:3909`) |
| Root still 100% full after moving `/var/lib/docker` [17] | `/var/lib/containerd` is a separate store | Relocate **both**, add to fstab, verify with `df -h` (`:1323`) |
| `no space left on device` mid-run [18, 20] | Estimate ignored image bytes and build cache | `imageBytes × 2 + volumes + 2 GiB`; re-checked before the image phase with a per-image budget (`:4036`, `:4049`) |
| A 20 GB volume sat unused while root filled [19] | Attached but unformatted/unmounted | `findUnusedDisks` (`:1198`) + `verifyBlank` (`:1255`) + format/mount/relocate (`:1298`) |
| Guest agent stopped responding during a build [21] | 1 vCPU / 2 GB starved by a .NET + Astro build | The engine's **SSH channel is authoritative**, never the guest agent; small-target warning at `:3671` |
| "Sites actually serving: 4/4" with six domains dark [22] | The denominator was "domains we chose to publish" — 100% by construction | Denominator is the **source's own** vhosts (`:3421`); unserved names are named and force `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` |
| Probe passed on the Apache2 default page [23] | Only the status code was checked | Body fetched; distro default pages and near-empty 2xx rejected (`:2137`) |
| Visitors saw a full-page security warning [24] | The probe used `-k`, so a wrong cert was invisible | Cert read with SNI via `openssl s_client`, CN/SAN matched (`:2163`, `:2185`) |
| Apache `enabled + failed`, quiet until a reboot [27] | Two web servers, one port 80 | Others stopped, disabled and **masked**, with the `unmask` command printed (`:2648`) |
| Progress frozen ten minutes at 89% [28] | `apt-get install certbot` with no output | `withHeartbeat` (`:485`) emits a line every ~45 s naming what is still running and for how long |
| Pre-flight demanded 83.6 GB for a 12 GB move | Wizard and worker both added the Docker allowance | **Fixed** (`05e6609`… commit `05e6605`): `items.totalBytes` is files-only, contract documented at both ends |
| Wizard said 11 GB, engine needed 47.8 GB | The earlier version of the same bug — cost ~40 GB of one-way purchased disk | Same fix. **No test asserts the two agree** |
| Ticked "use my volume for Docker" and it was ignored | The volume is only actually used when the pre-flight is *tight* | `migrate-real.ts:3378-3421`; the wizard already said "{n} GB on your volume" |
| Migration says COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES — now what? | One or more source domains do not serve here, or a unit is unhealthy, or the inventory was unreadable | The reasons are in `Migration.items.results`; see the re-run runbook. Do **not** move DNS for a named unserved domain |
| TLS was never re-issued after DNS moved | `runPostCutoverTls` has **no caller** — the enqueue line lives only in a comment | Queue it by hand (re-run runbook step 4). **Still broken** |

## Troubleshooting — mail

| Symptom | Cause | Fix / where to look |
|---|---|---|
| Mail is rejected / lands in spam | Broken forward-confirmed rDNS: `PTR[51.79.162.96] = ns5002569…`, the OVH default | Fix the PTR in the OVH panel. Verify with `dig -x … @1.1.1.1` — **never** bare, `/etc/hosts` answers |
| A deliverability check says a record is missing that is definitely published | The check used the system/default resolver instead of the zone's authority | Aim `dig` at `@$NS`. Domain-ownership verification (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:464`) has this bug **today** |
| "No mailbox connected" but the mailbox exists on the server | A Mailcow mailbox with no `Mailbox` row is invisible to `resolveMailbox` | `discoverMailboxes` (`lib/mail/imap.ts:126`) adopts orphans for **verified** subscriptions |
| Another customer took over our email domain | Duplicate check was scoped to the caller; no unique constraints; Mailcow keys by address | **Fixed** — global duplicate check (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:269`) and `Mailbox.address @unique` (`schema.prisma:674`) |
| DKIM row is blank in the DNS panel | Mailcow has not generated a key for that domain. **This repo never calls `/add/dkim`** | Generation is a side effect of `mcCreateDomain`; re-run domain creation, then re-read |
| Attachment upload fails well under the advertised limit | Next's server-action body limit vs base64 inflation (~33%) | `next.config.ts` `experimental.serverActions.bodySizeLimit`; caps at `lib/actions-mail.ts:318` |
| Display name / Reply-To not applied | Historically saved and never used | **Fixed** — applied at `lib/actions-mail.ts:468-487` |
| Auto-reply / forwarding do nothing | Historically store-only, no sieve | **Fixed** — real Mailcow sieve, pushed **before** the DB write (`lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:416`); status read back from the live script (`:361`) |
| Admin changed the MX host / SPF include and nothing changed | Both keys are **saved and read by nothing**; real values hardcoded | `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:36`, `:41`. **Still broken** |
| Nxeon-registered domain's mailboxes never go live | Nothing publishes MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC at name.com for in-account domains — only A records | `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:283`. **Still broken**, and the UI promises otherwise |
| Signature missing on a sent message | The signature is appended **in the browser**, not by `sendMessage` | `components/customer/mail/Composer.tsx:165` |

## Troubleshooting — SSL, domains and DNS

| Symptom | Cause | Fix / where to look |
|---|---|---|
| Certificate shows ACTIVE with an expiry but no cert exists | Simulated issuance wrote `ACTIVE` + `now + 90d` and notified success | **Fixed** — the fall-through throws (`worker/ssl.ts:692`) and the expiry is read off disk (`:434`, `:303`) |
| Certificates lapse at 90 days with no warning | `sslRenewalSweep` and `sslReconcileSweep` are written and **never called** | `worker/index.ts:18` imports only `sslIssue`. **Still broken** — wire the sweep, or renew in-guest |
| A row is stuck `ISSUING` and cannot be deleted | Delete was blocked on status rather than a live job | Now only blocks while a job is genuinely `RUNNING` (`lib/actions-ssl.ts:292`) |
| `certbot … Invalid response … 404` | DNS does not point here, or Cloudflare's orange cloud is on | Grey-cloud it; platform-written A records are always `proxied: false` (`lib/cloudflare-point.ts:159`) |
| Cannot issue `*.example.com` | HTTP-01 cannot validate a wildcard | DNS-01 with the customer's Cloudflare token — exists only in the migration engine (`migrate-real.ts:2991`) |
| Cloudflare connect fails with "invalid scope" | The **code default** scope (`lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts:59`) is a value Cloudflare rejects | The working value lives only in `.env:39`. Any deploy that loses it reintroduces this |
| Cloudflare connection silently stops working | The working scope omits `offline_access`, so **no refresh token is ever issued** | `resolveCloudflareToken` returns `CF_RECONNECT` at `:332`. The customer must reconnect manually; there is no prompt |
| Admin shows 0% domain markup, customers charged 25% | The key had a `"0"` default and **nothing read it** | **Fixed** — read at `lib/registrar.ts:89`, default corrected to `"25"` (`lib/settings.ts:56`) |
| "WHOIS privacy: enabled" but the registrar never heard | `whoisPrivacy` is persist-only, no registrar call | `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:133-152`. **Still broken** |
| Domain expiry looks wrong | If the registrar returned no expiry, a local date is computed and shown identically | `lib/actions-domains.ts:199`, `:216`. **Still present** |
| Transfer-in CTA is missing entirely | Gated on `transfersAvailable()` — invisible if the registrar env goes missing, with no error | `lib/registrar.ts:18` |
| The public DNS-lookup tool disagrees with reality | `new Resolver()` with no `setServers` → resolv.conf | `app/api/tools/dns/route.ts:35` |

## Troubleshooting — backups, volumes and storage

| Symptom | Cause | Fix / where to look |
|---|---|---|
| A customer's backup click deleted the platform's DR copy of their VM | `pruneBackups` selected victims on `vmid` alone, across the shared storage | **Fixed, three layers.** Platform archives live in `/tank/backup/platform`, outside every PVE storage, so they have no `volid` and are **not addressable**. `lib/proxmox.ts:403-437` |
| Backups pile up past the limit | `pruneBackups` only ever runs after a **successful** new backup | A failed backup or disabled schedule leaves archives. There is still no standalone retention sweep for customer archives |
| Customer ticked "Daily backups" and got none | `addons.dailyBackup` was write-only; the scheduler keys off `autoBackup` | **Fixed** at the point of sale — `lib/order.ts:258` |
| "Restore failed — your server is unaffected" | The message is shared with backups; for a restore it is **false** — the VM is already stopped and the disk overwritten | `worker/restore.ts:103`; check `verbFor` in `components/customer/BackupControls.tsx:16` |
| No alert although a server has never been backed up | `worker/monitor.ts:203` can only alert when `count > 0` and the listing was reachable | Both zero-backups and a failed listing are **silent**. Read `/tank/backup/status/*.json` by hand |
| Restore verification is green but a guest has no archive | `verify-restore.sh` writes `"ok":true` even with non-empty `WARNINGS` | Read the `warnings` field, not just `ok` |
| Off-site backups appear to run and do nothing | Not configured — and it says so honestly | Set `OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE` or `OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET` in `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env`. `/tank` is currently a single point of failure |
| Detach says "could NOT be detached safely" | Something in the guest has the filesystem mounted | The notification **names the dependents**. Stop them and retry. `worker/volumes.ts:1189` |
| An in-use volume cannot be force-detached | The worker supports `payload.ackInUse`; **nothing sets it** | No UI exists for the override the notification tells the customer to use. **Still broken** |
| "Attach" refuses: holds data on another server | `volume.serverId` is pinned and detach does not always clear it | Volumes are effectively **not portable** once they hold data. `lib/actions-volumes.ts:129` |
| Volume attached but unusable | `probeDevice` found a non-blank disk and refused to format it | Deliberate. `worker/volumes.ts:601` — it will not overwrite an unknown filesystem |
| Deploy refused for capacity | `capacityCheck` compares summed **plan** RAM across all nodes against a hardcoded 64 GB host ceiling | `lib/capacity.ts:15`, `:69`. It is a model, not a measurement, and it gates deploys |
