enum NodeStatus {
  ONLINE
  OFFLINE
  MAINTENANCE
}

/// A Proxmox hypervisor the platform can provision onto. The primary node
/// represents this host; additional nodes are onboarded via scripts/onboard-node.sh.
model Node {
  id            String     @id @default(cuid())
  name          String     @unique
  pveNode       String     // Proxmox node name (e.g. ns5002569)
  apiUrl        String     // https://host:8006
  tokenId       String
  tokenSecret   String
  publicIp      String
  bridge        String     @default("vmbr1")
  subnetPrefix  String     @default("10.20.0.") // /24 NAT subnet prefix
  ipStart       Int        @default(100)
  ipEnd         Int        @default(250)
  sshPortStart  Int        @default(20000)
  sshPortEnd    Int        @default(29999)
  natChain      String     @default("NXEON_FWD")
  storageNvme   String     @default("vmdata")
  storageHdd    String     @default("vmdata-hdd")
  capacityRamMB Int        @default(56000)
  isPrimary     Boolean    @default(false)
  enabled       Boolean    @default(true)
  status        NodeStatus @default(ONLINE)
  lastSeenAt    DateTime?
  createdAt     DateTime   @default(now())
  servers       Server[]
}

enum InvoiceStatus {
  OPEN
  PAID
  VOID
  REFUNDED
}

model Invoice {
  id          String        @id @default(cuid())
  number      Int           @unique @default(autoincrement())
  userId      String
  user        User          @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  amountCents Int
  taxCents    Int           @default(0)
  status      InvoiceStatus @default(OPEN)
  // How much of this invoice has already been refunded. Refunds used to be bound
  // to nothing: `refundPayment` took only (userId, amount) and picked its Stripe
  // target as "most recent top-up, any amount" — so refunding a $24 March invoice
  // issued $24 against the customer's $200 July top-up, the invoice stayed PAID,
  // and the next admin refunded it again. Tracking it here lets the action refuse
  // to exceed the original and mark the invoice REFUNDED.
  refundedCents Int         @default(0)
  description String
  lineItems   Json          // [{ description, qty, unitCents, amountCents }]
  periodStart DateTime?
  periodEnd   DateTime?
  paidAt      DateTime?
  createdAt   DateTime      @default(now())
}

// ---- Growth: coupons / promo codes ----
enum CouponKind {
  PERCENT      // value = percent 1-100 (discount on order/topup)
model Migration {
  id              String    @id @default(cuid())
  userId          String
  serverId        String    // target Nxeon server
  sourceHost      String
  sourcePort      Int       @default(22)
  sourceUser      String    @default("root")
  sourcePasswordEnc String? // encrypted source SSH password; CLEARED once the job finishes
  items           Json?     // what to move: { paths: string[], databases: [{engine,name,user,passEnc}] }
  status          String    @default("PENDING") // PENDING | RUNNING | DONE | FAILED
  progress        Int       @default(0)         // 0..100
  step            String?   // human-readable current step
  log             String?   // tail of the migration log
  lastError       String?
  createdAt       DateTime  @default(now())
  finishedAt      DateTime?

  @@index([userId])
  @@index([serverId])
}

// ---- Outbound abuse detection (protects IP reputation + the platform) ----
model AbuseAlert {
  id         String    @id @default(cuid())
  serverId   String
  userId     String
  kind       String    // BANDWIDTH_SPIKE | SMTP_ABUSE | PORT_SCAN | OTHER
  severity   String    @default("MEDIUM") // LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH
  detail     String
  metric     Json?     // measured values (e.g. { mbps, windowSec, bytes })
  status     String    @default("OPEN") // OPEN | ACKNOWLEDGED | RESOLVED | ACTIONED
  createdAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  resolvedAt DateTime?

  @@index([status, createdAt])
  @@index([serverId])
}

// ============================================================================
// Control panel (cPanel/Plesk-style VPS management over SSH)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Every row is scoped to a Server + owning userId. Side-effecting work (writing
// nginx vhosts, creating DBs, installing apps, editing crontab, service control)
// runs in the worker over SSH (worker/websites|databases|apps|services.ts),
// gated by SANDBOX exactly like the rest of the platform. Quick reads (lists,
// service status, process snapshot) are served straight from these tables /
// synthetic sandbox data. `serverId` uses a cascade so a server teardown cleans
// up its panel rows.
// ============================================================================

/// A website (nginx server block + docroot under /var/www) the customer added
model ServerDiskSample {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  serverId   String
  ts         DateTime @default(now())
  usedBytes  BigInt
  totalBytes BigInt

  @@index([serverId, ts])
}

model Improvement {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  batchId      String?  // groups one nightly scan
  category     String   // bug | feature | error | enhancement | security | performance
  severity     String   @default("medium") // low | medium | high | critical
  title        String
  summary      String   // one-to-two sentence concise description (owner reads this)
  detail       String?  // longer optional detail, collapsed by default
  source       String?  // nightly-scan | feedback | error-log | bug-report | audit
  effort       String?  // S | M | L
  filesHint    String?  // suggested files/areas to change
  status       String   @default("PROPOSED") // PROPOSED | APPROVED | DECLINED | IN_PROGRESS | DONE
  resolvedNote String?
  ownerNote    String?  // owner's instructions for how to handle this item
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt
  @@index([status])
  @@index([batchId])
}

# Part VI — Honest status

## The recurring defect — reporting an outcome nobody verified

**This codebase has one bug, and it has shipped many times.** A surface reports an outcome it never
verified. Every variant below is the same shape:

```
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │  do something  ──►  ASSUME it worked  ──►  write success             │
 │                                            notify the customer       │
 │                                            render it as fact         │
 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    ▲
                    └── the missing step: ASK THE WORLD WHETHER IT WORKED
```

Five instances found on a single day:

| Instance | What was claimed | What was true |
|---|---|---|
| SSL | Certificate rows `ACTIVE` with a `now + 90d` expiry and *"Your Let's Encrypt certificate is active"* | No certbot ran. No certificate existed anywhere on the box |
| Game settings | *"Game settings applied on `<hostname>`"* | Nothing was written to the VM; the `(sandbox)` qualifier was suppressed because `SANDBOX` is false in production |
| Migration | `Sites actually serving: 4/4` | Six of the customer's domains were dark. The denominator was "domains we chose to publish", so the metric was 100% **by construction** |
| Domain markup | Admin panel displayed **0%** | Customers were charged **25%**. Nothing read the setting at all |
| Auto-suspend kill switch | An admin toggle that appeared to be saved | It was saved, and read by nothing |

**The four shapes to watch for**, because they recur:

1. **Simulated-success fall-through.** A feature flag is unset, so the code takes a branch that writes
   the success value without doing the work.
2. **Saved-but-unread.** An admin sets a value; nothing consumes it. Worse when a panel *states* what
   it affects.
3. **Env-vs-setting split.** The value is read from `process.env` while the admin edits a `Setting`
   row (or vice versa). Both the domain markup and `referral_reward_cents` are this.
4. **A metric that cannot fail.** A denominator chosen from the numerator's own set; a shell command
   ending `; true`; a status written outside the `if` that decided it.

**Two things this project got right, and they are the pattern to copy:**

- **Fail loudly instead of simulating.** `worker/ssl.ts:692` and `worker/game-config.ts:86` now
  *throw* with an explanation naming the flag, rather than writing a success. The customer sees a
  failure with a real reason. That is strictly better than a comforting lie, even though it means the
  feature is visibly unavailable.
- **Delete the control you cannot enforce.** `Membership.areas` was written, echoed back as saved, and
  read by nothing. Rather than leave it, the control was **removed** and the customer is told what a
  membership actually grants (`lib/actions-teams.ts:22-26`).

And the meta-lesson, from `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md:115-127`, about failure #25 recurring four
months after it was written up as #13 in the same file:

> **A documented fix is not a fix. Nothing in the engine read this file.** … a failure mode that has
> been observed twice belongs in code, and a field note describing a fix nobody implemented is worth
> approximately nothing.

Which is why **this manual is not a substitute for a check**. If you find yourself documenting a
behaviour rather than asserting it, ask whether a test or a guard would be a better place to put the
sentence.

## Known gaps — the honest inventory

Verified against the tree at the time of writing. Several agents edit this repo concurrently, so
re-check anything before you rely on it. Classification:

- **WORKS** — verified end to end.
- **SIMULATED** — produces a fabricated result.
- **UNVERIFIED SUCCESS** — does real work but reports success without checking it.
- **SAVED-BUT-UNREAD** — written by a UI, consumed by nothing.
- **DEAD** — implemented, never called.
- **PARTIAL** — real but incomplete or overstated.

### Still not true — ranked by what it would cost a customer or admin

**1. One-click apps install one app.** *UNVERIFIED SUCCESS — active, customer-facing.*
`worker/apps.ts:151`: only WordPress has an installer. Ghost, Nextcloud, Joomla and Matomo get a
vhost, a database and an `index.html` saying *"<App> is ready to install"*. The row is then set
`ACTIVE` unconditionally (`:171`) and the customer is told *"Your Ghost site is live at {url}. Admin
credentials were shown once at install."* (`:180`) — with credentials generated at
`lib/actions-apps.ts:200` that no software exists to accept. **This is the worst live instance of the
recurring defect.**

**2. Game auto-update cannot fail.** *UNVERIFIED SUCCESS — runs unattended every 6 hours.*
`worker/game-update.ts:60` returns `set -e; ${steam}${restart}; true`. steamcmd is `|| true` and
skipped entirely when absent; every restart branch is `|| true`; the command ends `; true`. The remote
command **cannot** exit non-zero, so `:133` always fires *"The latest server update was applied and
the service was restarted."*

**3. Nothing renews SSL certificates.** *DEAD.* `sslRenewalSweep` (`worker/ssl.ts:929`),
`sslReconcileSweep` (`:836`) and the `sslSweep` wrapper (`:1058`) are fully written — 21-day lead,
served-state verification, `autoRenew` honoured, LE rate caps, backoff ladder, stranded-row cleanup —
and **never called**. `worker/index.ts:18` imports only `sslIssue`. Every certificate issued today
lapses at 90 days with no warning, no `EXPIRED` transition, and no cleanup of stranded
`PENDING`/`ISSUING` rows. `SslCertificate.autoRenew` is written and, until this is wired, read by
nothing.

**4. There is no UI to save a card, so renewal auto-charge can never fire.** *DEAD.*
The engine is real and wired (`worker/billing.ts:28-43`), but
`lib/actions-payment-method.ts` — `startCardSetup` `:46`, `finalizeCardSetup` `:72`,
`removeSavedCard` `:101`, `settleOutstanding` `:127` — has **zero callers** in `app/` or
`components/`. Every renewal is wallet-only; a customer with an empty wallet goes straight to
grace → suspend, which is exactly the outcome the dunning engine was built to prevent.

**5. Post-cutover TLS is never retried.** *DEAD.* `runPostCutoverTls` (`worker/migrate.ts:260`) is
reached only via `payload.phase === "tls"`, and the enqueue line exists **only inside a comment**
(`:258`). `pointMigrationDns` does not trigger it. So names that could not be issued at migration time
— the normal case, since DNS has not moved yet — are never retried.
`issueMigrationCertificates` (`migrate-real.ts:3236`) exists for this and still effectively has no
caller.

**6. Migration simulation still reports success when the flag is off.** *SIMULATED — dormant.*
Unlike SSL and game-config, `worker/migrate.ts:453` falls through to a synthetic branch that fabricates
step results, writes `status: "DONE"` (`:533`) and notifies *"Migration to X completed"* (`:536`). Its
sleep timings were written for the non-sandbox case. `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION=1` today, so it is
dormant — **a single lost `.env` line re-creates the original lie on the flagship feature.** The same
applies to the four `ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL` workers (`websites.ts:39`, `apps.ts:81`, `databases.ts:35`,
`services.ts:34`).

**7. Nxeon-registered domains get no mail DNS.** *PARTIAL — the UI promises otherwise.*
`components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:260-263` says a domain registered with Nxeon has *"its mail DNS
managed for you — mailboxes go live automatically."* Nothing publishes MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC at name.com:
`lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:283` only ever adds A records.

**8. `email_mx_host` and `email_spf_include` change nothing.** *SAVED-BUT-UNREAD — and the panel makes
an explicit false claim.* `components/admin/settings/GeneralPanel.tsx:26` says *"Shown in the customer
business-email DNS setup panel"*; `:34` says *"Rendered as `v=spf1 include:<value> ~all`"*. Neither is
true. The real values are hardcoded (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:36`, `:41`), and the admin defaults
(`mx.nxeon.email`, `_spf.nxeon.email`) differ from them, so the panel makes correctly-configured mail
look broken.

**9. Domain-ownership verification uses the wrong resolver.** *PARTIAL.*
`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:464`, `:474` use the top-level `resolveTxt`/`resolveMx`, i.e.
`/etc/resolv.conf` and OVH's cache, not the zone's authority. A customer who has just published
`_nxeon-verify` can be told it is not there. `lib/mail/deliverability.ts` does it correctly and is the
model to copy. Same bug in `app/api/tools/dns/route.ts:35` (no `setServers`) and
`app/api/tools/my-ip/route.ts:23` (`reverse` on the default resolver).

**10. There is no PTR / reverse-DNS check anywhere.** *Missing.* `checkDeliverability` covers only
`mx | spf | dkim | dmarc` (`lib/mail/deliverability.ts:41`) — despite the motivating incident being a
*reverse* lookup. And the correct checker `checkEmailDeliverability`
(`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:523`) has **no caller**, so there is no UI entry point at all.
`components/admin/MailAnalytics.tsx:135-148`'s "DNS & DMARC" card is static prose.

**11. Cloudflare connections cannot refresh.** *PARTIAL.* The working scope in `.env:39` omits
`offline_access`, so no refresh token is issued and every connection dies at `expiresAt`
(`lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts:332` → `CF_RECONNECT`) with no re-auth prompt. Separately, the **code
default** scope (`:59`) is a value Cloudflare rejects, so any deploy that loses that env var
reintroduces the "invalid scope" error.

**12. Backup monitoring is silent in the two cases that matter.** *PARTIAL.*
`worker/monitor.ts:203` can only alert when `count > 0` **and** the listing was reachable. A server
that has never been backed up, and a node whose backup listing failed (swallowed by a bare `catch {}`
at `lib/monitoring.ts:203`), both produce **no alert** — which is exactly the failure
`verify-restore.sh:7-11` documents. Compounding it: the status JSON the scripts write for
`/admin/backups` has **no reader and there is no such page**, and `verify-restore.sh` writes
`"ok":true` even with non-empty `WARNINGS` (`:122-127`).

**13. Off-site backups are inert.** *Not configured, honestly reported.* `/tank` is one pool in one
chassis. `offsite.json` says `configured:false`. A chassis loss loses every backup.

**14. A genuinely in-use volume cannot be force-detached.** *PARTIAL.* The worker supports
`payload.ackInUse` (`worker/volumes.ts:1147`) and the refusal notification tells the customer to
*"confirm the forced detach in the dashboard"* — **nothing sets it**. The escape hatch exists only in
the engine.

**15. Volumes are not portable.** *PARTIAL — marketing is stronger than the code.*
`lib/actions-volumes.ts:129` refuses attaching to any server other than `volume.serverId`, and detach
only clears it when the disk did not stay behind (`worker/volumes.ts:1154`).

**16. "Restore failed — your server is unaffected" is false for restores.** *UNVERIFIED SUCCESS,
inverted.* `components/customer/BackupControls.tsx` shares its failure copy between backup and
restore; by the time a restore fails, `worker/restore.ts:103-110` has stopped the VM and begun
overwriting the disk. Check `verbFor` (`:16`) before trusting it.

**17. Game settings are switched off and the copy has not caught up.** *PARTIAL.*
`ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG` is unset, so every production save now fails loudly — correct, but the feature is
non-functional, while `components/customer/GameSettings.tsx:72` still says *"Changes are queued and
applied to the server"*. Even on the real path nothing reads back
(`worker/game-config.ts:118-165`), and `:136` writes the `_appliedAt` marker even when
`outcome.ok === false`.

**18. Bandwidth metering is mid-integration.** *PARTIAL — landed during this session.*
`lib/bandwidth.ts` states two rules, and the second is not yet honoured on the surface it was written
for: `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:56` still sums the columns directly, so a partial period is
presented as authoritative. `bwUsageView` has no consumer. Separately,
the **automatic** abuse suspension in `worker/abuse.ts` does not set `suspendReason: "ABUSE"` — only
the manual admin path does.

**19. The capacity gauge is a model, and it gates deploys.** *PARTIAL.*
`lib/capacity.ts:15` uses `NXEON_HOST_RAM_MB ?? 64000`; the variable is unset. `capacitySnapshot()`
sums **plan** RAM across servers on **all** nodes against that single-host ceiling, while the platform
is multi-node. It is shown to customers at `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx:34` and gates deploys via
`capacityCheck` (`:69`).

**20. The public status page reports `web` as a constant.** *PARTIAL.*
`lib/monitoring.ts:326` hardcodes `web: { status: "operational" }`, rolled into `overallStatus`
(`:335`) and rendered on `/status` under *"Component states above are checked live"*
(`app/status/page.tsx:126`). Tautological for the page itself; false for the marketing site and admin
console, neither of which is probed. `db`, `worker` and `proxmox` **are** genuinely measured.

**21. "Server is ready" is Proxmox-task-deep only.** *PARTIAL.* `worker/index.ts:318` writes `RUNNING`
and `:323` notifies with an `ssh root@…` line straight after `waitForTask(startUpid)`. The cloud-init
snippet write at `:274` is `.catch`'d, so a server can be reported ready with no cloud-init applied.

**22. The API token scope badge contradicts the auth layer.** *PARTIAL.*
`components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx:268` renders an empty-scopes token as **"read"** while
`lib/api-auth.ts:72` treats empty scopes as **full access**. Harmless only because the public API is
read-only; the footgun is documented in place at `lib/api-auth.ts:78-92`.

**23. WHOIS privacy never reaches the registrar.** *SAVED-BUT-UNREAD.*
`lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:133-152` writes the DB flag and makes no registrar call; the domain
page ticks a green checklist item off it.

**24. Domain expiry can be locally invented.** *UNVERIFIED SUCCESS.*
`lib/actions-domains.ts:199`, `:216`: `expiresAt: info.expires ?? new Date(now + years×365d)`. The
same shape as the old SSL bug, small blast radius because the `Domain` table is empty.

**25. Tax is configured and never charged.** *SAVED-BUT-UNREAD.* `applyTaxFromSettings` has one call
site — an admin MRR display (`app/admin/products/page.tsx:93`). No invoice creator passes `taxCents`.

**26. `referral_reward_cents` is read by nothing.** *ENV-VS-SETTING SPLIT.* Validated in
`lib/actions-settings.ts:141`; the reward path reads `process.env.REFERRAL_REWARD_CENTS`
(`lib/growth.ts:14`).

**27. Coupon codes on card top-ups.** *Verify before promising.* The cookie was read only by the demo
gateway, which refuses in production; the Checkout session carried no `discounts` and the credit used
`amount_total` verbatim.

**28. Ten more admin settings with no reader.** *SAVED-BUT-UNREAD.*

| Key | Contradicted by |
|---|---|
| `brand_name`, `brand_tagline`, `footer_text` | "Nxeon" hardcoded throughout |

**The inverse defect:** `worker/index.ts:229` and `:476` read **`dedicated_ip_default`**, which is not
in `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS` and appears in no panel — a provisioning knob no admin can see or set, silently
defaulting to `true`.

**29. `test/migration-gate.test.ts` does not exist.** *A verification claim that was never verified.*
`migrate-real.ts:2217` says the scoring rule *"is exercised by `test/migration-gate.test.ts` instead of
only ever being exercised by a real customer's cutover."* It is not. There is no migration test at all,
no rehearsal harness, and no CI. **The next customer migration is the gate's first real test.**

**30. Structural gaps.**

- **The worker is a strictly serial single-job queue.** No per-type concurrency. A 24-minute migration
  blocks every other customer's SSL issuance. There is no queue-position ETA in most UIs.
- **No server-side `expectedCents` binding** on checkout, so a wizard left open across a promo
  boundary or an admin price change can still charge something other than what was displayed.
- **No admin migration surface and no re-run path.**
- **Teams confer no cross-account access**; no dashboard page is org-scoped; there is no shared
  billing.
- **`prisma db push`, not versioned migrations** — schema rollback is destructive by hand.
- **Proxmox `:8006` and host SSH are in the public accept set** (`scripts/firewall.nft:28`, `:33`).
- **Platform-key mode for the AI builder is unavailable** — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset, no usage meter,
  no per-plan quota. BYOK only.
- **`ROADMAP.md` has been wrong in both directions** — it once marked the dunning engine `[x]` when
  none existed while listing shipped work as outstanding. Trust this document and `git log` over it.

### Things that are genuinely, verifiably true

Worth stating explicitly, so the list above is not read as "nothing works":

- Provisioning, resize, disk expansion, snapshots, backups and restores all really drive Proxmox.
- Every SSH command in `worker/databases.ts`, `worker/services.ts` and `worker/websites.ts` checks its
  exit code and throws; `nginx -t` gates the reload.
- `scripts/backup-vms.sh:139`, `:169` checks `vzdump`'s exit status **and** asserts an archive actually
  appeared in the last 6 hours before reporting success.
- Restore verification genuinely restores the newest DB dump into a scratch database and asserts row
  counts.
- `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts:85-99` — payment captured but provisioning failed writes `FAILED` and tells
  the customer honestly. There is no success-on-error path.
- `lib/actions-domains.ts:191-230` never refunds blind; it calls `verifyRegistration` first.
- Every synthetic value elsewhere is strictly `if (SANDBOX)`-gated and self-labelled —
  `lib/cloudflare-point.ts` even returns `simulated: true` and the UI prints "pretended to point…".
- `lib/analytics.ts` is real `Visit`-table aggregation. `lib/server-metrics.ts:28` is real Proxmox
  `rrddata`, so the `netin`/`netout` charts in `components/customer/MetricsPanel.tsx:149` are genuinely
  measured.
- The migration engine never mutates the source, always scrubs its secrets, and never leaves the
  target's web server unable to start.

but `lib/actions-payment-method.ts` — `startCardSetup` `:46`, `finalizeCardSetup` `:72`,
`removeSavedCard` `:101`, `settleOutstanding` `:127` — has **zero callers** in `app/` or
`components/`. Every renewal is therefore wallet-only, and a customer with an empty wallet goes
straight to grace → suspend: precisely the outcome the dunning engine was built to prevent. This is
the single highest-value wiring job outstanding.

**2. The hardened firewall is in the file, not in the kernel.** *NOT APPLIED.*
`scripts/firewall.nft` has been rewritten to restrict the two administrative ports —
`define ADMIN_PORTS = { 22, 8006 }` (`:120`), accepted only from `@nxeon_admin_v4`/`@nxeon_admin_v6`
(`:190-191`) — and the comment at `:21-35` explains why: a successful login on `:8006` is
*"not 'a server gets hacked', it is 'the hosting company ends'"*. But the **live** ruleset still reads:

```
tcp dport { 22, 80, 443, 8006, 8080, 8443 } accept
```

So Proxmox's web UI and host SSH are reachable from the internet right now. Populate the admin sets and
apply with `scripts/firewall-safe-apply.sh` (it has a rollback timer — do not `nft -f` by hand over an
SSH session you cannot afford to lose).

**3. Game auto-update cannot fail.** *UNVERIFIED SUCCESS — runs unattended every 6 hours.*
`worker/game-update.ts:60` returns `set -e; ${steam}${restart}; true`. steamcmd is `|| true` (`:51`)
and skipped entirely when absent; every restart branch is `|| true` (`:59`); the command ends `; true`.
The remote command **cannot** exit non-zero, so `:134` always fires *"The latest server update was
applied and the service was restarted."* `worker/apps.ts` is now the model for how to fix this — it
proves the outcome with `verifyServing()` and fails the job with the real HTTP result.

**4. Post-cutover TLS is never retried.** *DEAD.* `runPostCutoverTls` (`worker/migrate.ts:260`) is
reached only via `payload.phase === "tls"`, and the enqueue line exists **only inside a comment**
(`:258`) — a repo-wide grep for `phase: "tls"` returns that comment and nothing else.
`pointMigrationDns` does not trigger it. So names that could not be issued at migration time — the
normal case, since DNS has not moved yet — are never retried.
`issueMigrationCertificates` (`migrate-real.ts:3236`) exists for exactly this and still effectively has
no caller. Until it is wired, closing the loop means queueing the job by hand (see the migration
re-run runbook).

**5. Migration simulation still reports success when the flag is off.** *SIMULATED — dormant.*
Unlike SSL and game-config, which now throw, `worker/migrate.ts:452` falls through to a synthetic
branch that fabricates step results, writes `status: "DONE"` / `step: "Completed"` (`:533`) and
notifies *"Migration to X completed"* (`:536`). Its sleep timings were written for the non-sandbox
case. `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION=1` today, so it is dormant — **one lost `.env` line re-creates the
original lie on the flagship feature.** The same fall-through shape applies to the four
`ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL` workers (`websites.ts:39`, `apps.ts:81`, `databases.ts:35`, `services.ts:34`).

**6. Nxeon-registered domains get no mail DNS.** *PARTIAL — the UI promises otherwise.*
`components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:261` tells the customer that a domain registered with Nxeon has
*"its mail DNS managed for you — mailboxes go live automatically."* Nothing publishes
MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC at name.com: `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:283` only ever adds A records. Their mail
will not work, and the panel says it will.

**7. `email_mx_host` and `email_spf_include` change nothing.** *SAVED-BUT-UNREAD — and the panel makes
an explicit false claim about its own effect.* `components/admin/settings/GeneralPanel.tsx:26` says
*"Shown in the customer business-email DNS setup panel"*; `:34` says *"Rendered as
`v=spf1 include:<value> ~all`"*. Neither is true. The real values are hardcoded at
`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:36` (`mail.nxeon.cloud`) and `:41` (`nxeon.cloud`), while the admin
fields default to `mx.nxeon.email` and `_spf.nxeon.email` — so the panel makes correctly-configured
mail look misconfigured, and editing either field does nothing.

**8. Domain-ownership verification uses the wrong resolver.** *PARTIAL.*
`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:5` imports the top-level `resolveTxt`/`resolveMx`, used at `:464` and
`:474` — so verification runs against `/etc/resolv.conf` (OVH's cache), not the zone's authority. A
customer who has just published `_nxeon-verify` can be told it is not there.
`lib/mail/deliverability.ts` does it correctly and is the model to copy. The same bug is in
`app/api/tools/dns/route.ts:35` (a `Resolver` with no `setServers`) and
`app/api/tools/my-ip/route.ts:23` (`reverse` on the default resolver).

**9. There is no PTR / reverse-DNS check anywhere.** *Missing.* `checkDeliverability` covers only
`mx | spf | dkim | dmarc` (`lib/mail/deliverability.ts:41`) — despite the motivating incident being a
*reverse* lookup. And the correct checker `checkEmailDeliverability`
(`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:523`) has **no caller**, so there is no UI entry point at all.
`components/admin/MailAnalytics.tsx:135-148`'s "DNS & DMARC" card is static prose, not a check.

**10. Cloudflare connections cannot refresh.** *PARTIAL.* The working scope in `.env:39` omits
`offline_access`, so Cloudflare issues no refresh token and every connection dies at `expiresAt`
(`lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts:332` → `CF_RECONNECT`) with no re-auth prompt. Separately the **code
default** scope (`:59`) is a value Cloudflare rejects, so any deploy that loses that env var
reintroduces the "invalid scope" error a customer hit three times.

**11. Backup monitoring is silent in the two cases that matter.** *PARTIAL.*
`worker/monitor.ts:203` can only alert "stale" when `count > 0` **and** the listing was reachable. A
server that has never been backed up, and a node whose backup listing failed (swallowed by a bare
`catch {}` at `lib/monitoring.ts:203`), both produce **no alert** — which is exactly the failure
`scripts/verify-restore.sh:7-11` was written after. Compounding it: the status JSON those scripts write
"for `/admin/backups`" has **no reader and there is no such page**, and `verify-restore.sh` writes
`"ok":true` even with a non-empty `warnings` field (`:122-127`), so a guest with no archive at all still
reads as OK unless you look at `warnings`.

**12. Off-site backups are inert.** *Not configured, honestly reported.* `/tank` is one pool in one
chassis; `offsite.json` says `configured:false`. A chassis loss loses every backup, including the
platform's own disaster-recovery set. Set `OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE` or `OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET` in
`/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env`.

**13. A genuinely in-use volume cannot be force-detached.** *PARTIAL.* The worker supports an informed
override via `payload.ackInUse` (`worker/volumes.ts:1147`) and the refusal notification tells the
customer to *"confirm the forced detach in the dashboard"* — but **nothing sets it**: not
`lib/actions-volumes.ts`, not `components/customer/Volumes.tsx`. The escape hatch exists only in the
engine, and the notification points at a control that does not exist.

**14. Volumes are not portable.** *PARTIAL — the framing is stronger than the code.*
`lib/actions-volumes.ts:129` refuses attaching to any server other than `volume.serverId`, and detach
only clears it when the disk did not stay behind (`worker/volumes.ts:1154`). Once a volume holds data it
is effectively pinned to its first server.

**15. "Restore failed — your server is unaffected" is false for restores.** *UNVERIFIED SUCCESS,
inverted.* `components/customer/BackupControls.tsx:134` renders `{verb} failed — your server is
unaffected` and `:147` adds *"No changes were made to your running server. You can safely try again."*
— with `verbFor` (`:16`) returning `"Restore"` for `BACKUP_RESTORE`. By the time a restore fails,
`worker/restore.ts:103-110` has already stopped the VM and begun overwriting its disk. **The most
reassuring message in the product appears in its most destructive failure case.**

**16. Game settings are switched off and the copy has not caught up.** *PARTIAL.*
`ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG` is unset, so every production save now fails loudly (`worker/game-config.ts:86`)
— correct, but the feature is non-functional while
`components/customer/GameSettings.tsx:72` still says *"Changes are queued and applied to the server"*
and `:127` *"Settings queued for apply."* Even on the real path nothing reads back
(`worker/game-config.ts:118-165`), and `:136` writes the `_appliedAt` marker even when
`outcome.ok === false`.

**17. The capacity gauge is a model, and it gates deploys.** *PARTIAL.*
`lib/capacity.ts:15` uses `NXEON_HOST_RAM_MB ?? 64000` and the variable is unset, so the ceiling is a
hardcoded assumption about this specific box. `capacitySnapshot()` sums **plan** RAM across servers on
**all** nodes against that single-host ceiling, while the platform is multi-node. It is shown to
customers at `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx:34` and it **gates deploys** via `capacityCheck` (`:69`),
so the number is load-bearing.

**18. The public status page reports `web` as a constant.** *PARTIAL.*
`lib/monitoring.ts:326` hardcodes `web: { status: "operational", detail: "serving requests" }`, rolled
into `overallStatus` (`:335`) and rendered on `/status` under the claim *"Component states above are
checked live against the Nxeon platform"* (`app/status/page.tsx:126`). Tautological for the page
itself, and false for the marketing site and admin console, neither of which is probed. `db`, `worker`
and `proxmox` **are** genuinely measured.

**19. "Server is ready" is Proxmox-task-deep only.** *PARTIAL.* `worker/index.ts:318` writes `RUNNING`
and `:323` notifies with an `ssh root@…` line straight after `waitForTask(startUpid)`. That proves
Proxmox accepted the start — not that the guest booted, cloud-init ran, or sshd is listening. The
cloud-init snippet write at `:274` is `.catch`'d, so a server can be reported ready with no cloud-init
applied.

**20. The API token scope badge contradicts the auth layer.** *PARTIAL.*
`components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx:269` renders an empty-scopes token as **"read"** while
`lib/api-auth.ts:72` treats empty scopes as **full access**. Harmless only because the public API is
read-only; the footgun is documented in place at `lib/api-auth.ts:78-92`, and both halves must be dealt
with before any mutating endpoint ships.

**21. Domain expiry can be locally invented.** *UNVERIFIED SUCCESS.*
`lib/actions-domains.ts:199`, `:216`:
`expiresAt: info.expires ?? new Date(Date.now() + years × 365 × 86400_000)`. If the registrar returned
no expiry, the customer sees a computed date rendered identically to a registrar-confirmed one — the
same shape as the old SSL bug, with a small blast radius only because the `Domain` table is empty.

**22. Tax is configured and never charged.** *SAVED-BUT-UNREAD.* `applyTaxFromSettings` has exactly one
call site — `app/admin/products/page.tsx:93`, an admin MRR display. No invoice creator passes
`taxCents`, so every invoice renders Tax $0.00 while `tax_percent` sits editable in Settings.

**23. `referral_reward_cents` is read by nothing.** *ENV-VS-SETTING SPLIT.* Validated in
`lib/actions-settings.ts:141`; the reward path reads `process.env.REFERRAL_REWARD_CENTS`
(`lib/growth.ts:14`). Editing the admin field changes no payout — the same split that produced the
domain-markup bug.

**24. Thirteen more admin settings with no reader.** *SAVED-BUT-UNREAD.* Re-verified individually:

| Key | Contradicted by |
|---|---|
| `brand_name`, `brand_tagline`, `footer_text` | "Nxeon" hardcoded throughout |
| `support_email` | `components/marketing/ContactForm.tsx:4` hardcodes `support@nxeon.cloud` |
| `social_twitter` / `github` / `discord` / `linkedin` | `components/marketing/MarketingFooter.tsx:121`, `:127`, `:133` read `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SOCIAL_*`, also unset |
| `company_legal_name`, `company_address` | the panel says "shown on invoices"; `lib/invoices.ts:279` hardcodes the name and renders no address |
| `invoice_prefix` | `lib/invoices.ts:147` pads the number and renders `#N` |
| `default_term` | no reader — `lib/actions-settings.ts:44` even worries about "a `default_term` no charge path understands" |
| `whois_privacy_default` | no reader |
| `default_plan_slug` | the panel says "Pre-selected in the order wizard"; no preselect logic exists |

**The inverse defect:** `worker/index.ts:229` and `:476` read **`dedicated_ip_default`**, which is not
in `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS` and appears in no panel — a provisioning knob no admin can see or set, silently
defaulting to `true`.

**25. WHOIS privacy still never reaches the registrar** — but it now says so.
`lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:133-152` writes the DB flag and makes no registrar call, and the
action now returns an honest note: *"Preference saved. WHOIS privacy at {registrar} is provisioned at
registration — contact support to change it on a live domain."* That is the right shape. Check that the
domain page's checklist tick reflects the note rather than the raw flag.

**26. `test/migration-gate.test.ts` does not exist.** *A verification claim that was itself never
verified.* `worker/migrate-real.ts:2217` states the scoring rule *"is exercised by
`test/migration-gate.test.ts` instead of only ever being exercised by a real customer's cutover."* It
is not: `test/` holds `billing-terms`, `games`, `growth`, `rate-limit`, `totp`. There is no migration
test, no rehearsal harness, and no CI. **The next customer migration is the gate's first real test.**

**27. Structural gaps.**

- **The worker is a strictly serial single-job queue.** No per-type concurrency: a 24-minute migration
  blocks every other customer's SSL issuance. Most UIs show no queue position or ETA.
- **No server-side `expectedCents` binding** on checkout, so a wizard left open across a promo boundary
  or an admin price change mid-session can still charge something other than what was displayed. The

  `lib/wallet-split.ts` and `lib/proration.ts` exist to prevent.
- **Disk expansion bypasses `lib/proration.ts`**, reimplementing `monthlyCents × monthsRemaining` in
  three places (`lib/disk-expand.ts:124`, `components/customer/AddStorage.tsx:17`/`:66`). They agree
  today and nothing tests that they continue to.
- **No admin migration surface and no re-run path** for a failed migration.
- **Teams confer no cross-account access**; no dashboard page is org-scoped; there is no shared billing.
- **`prisma db push`, not versioned migrations** — schema rollback is a destructive manual act.
- **Platform-key mode for the AI builder is unavailable** — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset, no usage meter,
  no per-plan quota. BYOK only.
- **Documentation drift both ways.** `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md:136-143` and

  statuses where the code writes five. `ROADMAP.md` has been wrong in both directions — trust this
  document and `git log` over it.

`docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is rewritten: **4,993 lines / ~355 KB, 89 rendered sections, 51 tables, 90 ASCII code blocks, zero renderer faults.** Validated by running the actual `renderMarkdown` + section-splitter from `app/admin/docs/page.tsx`. ## H2 structure (89 sections)

**Part I — Orientation (7):** What Nxeon is · Architecture at a glance · Request lifecycle — browser to Proxmox · Job lifecycle — the worker queue · Environments — production, staging, and the .env contract · Codebase map

**Part II — Feature chapters (36):** Deploy wizard · Plans, terms and pricing · Wallet, checkout and the wallet/card split · Invoices · Renewals, card auto-charge and dunning · Suspension reasons — UNPAID vs ABUSE vs ADMIN · Server lifecycle · Resize and proration · Disk expansion · Block storage volumes · Backups — daily, keep 3, and platform vs customer archives · Snapshots and restore · **Server migration** (3 chapters: how a run unfolds / the verification gate and COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES / cutover, re-runs and the missing TLS retry) · Control panel · Web console and web terminal · SFTP and the file manager · Domains and the markup setting · Domain transfer-in · Cloudflare OAuth · SSL certificate lifecycle · Nxeon Mail · Business email hosting and DKIM · Deliverability checking — and why you must not trust this box's resolver · Game servers · Build with AI · Teams · Support · Notifications · API tokens · 2FA — and why `lib/totp-verify.ts` is a plain module · Growth · Bandwidth and abuse detection · Admin surfaces · RBAC

**Part III — Runbooks (8):** deploying · restarting safely (with the queue-check SQL and a decision tree) · reading worker logs · diagnosing a stuck job · re-running a failed migration · issuing a cert by hand · checking mail deliverability · rolling back

**Part IV — Troubleshooting (6):** billing · provisioning/worker · migration (all 28 field-note items) · mail · SSL/domains/DNS · backups/volumes/storage

**Part V — Reference (3):** Data model (60 models) · Env vars and feature flags · Scripts, units, timers

**Part VI — Honest status (2):** The recurring defect · Known gaps — the honest inventory (23 KB: 27 fixed-and-verified, 27 still-not-true, plus what genuinely works)

**Parts VII–VIII (25):** session log, this rewrite, then the original dated entries verbatim.

## Documented-but-wrong, corrected

- **Backups** were documented as weekly/keep-2; they are **daily/keep-3**, and platform archives now live in `/tank/backup/platform`, outside every PVE storage.
- **SSL** was documented as simulated on prod; `ENABLE_REAL_SSL=1`, the fall-through throws, expiries are read off disk.
- **Migration outcome→status** is documented as unwired in `MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md:136-143` and `migrate-real.ts:5251`; it **is** wired at `migrate.ts:412`. Flagged as stale in both places.
- Old §11's **Cloudflare scope default** is a value Cloudflare *rejects*; the working value lives only in `.env:39` and omits `offline_access`, so connections cannot refresh.
- Old §14 claimed a docs pass with diagrams; the file had **zero**.
- `schema.prisma:1009` lists four migration statuses; the code writes five.

## Four things I found that weren't in either audit

1. **The hardened firewall is in the file, not the kernel.** `scripts/firewall.nft:120` restricts `{22, 8006}` to admin sets; the **live** ruleset still reads `tcp dport { 22, 80, 443, 8006, 8080, 8443 } accept`.
2. **`sslRenewalSweep` was dead code** — reported; another agent wired it at `worker/index.ts:1098` mid-write.
3. **`email_mx_host`/`email_spf_include`** are saved-but-unread while the admin panel explicitly claims they drive the customer DNS panel — real values hardcoded at `actions-email-hosting.ts:36,41`.
4. **Backup status JSON has no reader** — the scripts write it "for `/admin/backups`", which does not exist.

Two process notes: the gap list was re-verified at the end and **four items moved out of it while I wrote** (app verification, SSL sweep, `bwUsageView`, coupon refusal) — those are now in the fixed table with evidence. And `HEAD` briefly contained my own half-finished draft, swept up by another agent's `git add -A`; I confirmed against `8e93b13` that no one else's prose was lost, and disclosed in Part VIII the only two edits made to the verbatim history (one retitle, one reflow forced by the renderer's list regex).
